title: Models únics versus models híbrids: l'impacte de l'educació esportiva associada a la pedagogia no lineal en un programa d'esport universitari
abstract: Evalúa un programa híbrido de educación deportiva y pedagogía no lineal frente a PNL sola en la formación inicial de docentes (fútbol universitario).
objective: Evaluar el impacto de un programa híbrido de educación deportiva (EE) + pedagogía no lineal (PNL) frente a uno solo de PNL en la motivación y satisfacción de futuros docentes.
design: Cuasi-experimental pre-post con dos grupos (MANOVA 2 × 2), 12 sesiones de fútbol en formación universitaria.
population: 67 futuros docentes de dos universidades españolas, divididos en un grupo EE+PNL y otro PNL.
method: Cuestionarios de motivación (teoría de la autodeterminación) y de satisfacción antes y después, con MANOVA y comparaciones por pares.
results: Solo el grupo híbrido mejoró de forma significativa la motivación intrínseca, redujo la desmotivación y aumentó la satisfacción (enseñanza, interacción y diversión; p entre .004 y .011); el grupo PNL no cambió.
conclusions: La EE complementa a la PNL y mejora los resultados motivacionales; hace falta formación adecuada en la universidad.
limitations: Diferencias iniciales entre grupos, muestra pequeña y medidas de autoinforme.
why: Muestra cómo implementar PNL en fútbol con alumnado y qué aporta combinarla con otros modelos.
practice: Puedes combinar roles y responsabilidades de los jugadores (EE) con tareas de PNL en tus sesiones.
summary: En 67 futuros docentes, combinar educación deportiva y PNL mejoró motivación y satisfacción; la PNL sola no produjo cambios.
why_background: Estudio de 2026 de INEFC (Sistemas Complejos y Deporte) sobre cómo enseñar PNL.

title: A spatio-temporal graph-based model for team sports analysis
abstract: Team sports represent complex phenomena characterized by both spatial and temporal dimensions, making their analysis inherently challenging. In this study, we examine team sports as complex systems, specifically focusing on the tactical aspects influenced by external constraints. To this end, we introduce a new generic graph-based model to analyze these phenomena. Specifically, we model a team sport’s attacking play as a directed path containing absolute and relative ball carrier-centered spatial information, temporal information, and semantic information. We first illustrate the expressiveness of our model on two team sports: basketball and rugby. Then, we focus on union rugby, aiming to validate two hypotheses regarding the impact of the pedagogy provided by the coach on the one hand, and the effect of the initial positioning of the defensive team on the other hand. Preliminary results from data collected on six-player rugby from several French clubs indicate notable effects of these constraints. The model is intended to be applied to other team sports and to validate additional hypotheses related to team coordination patterns.
objective: Proponer un modelo genérico basado en grafos para analizar las jugadas de ataque en deportes de equipo entendidos como sistemas complejos, y comprobar con él el efecto de la pedagogía del entrenador y del posicionamiento defensivo inicial.
design: Estudio metodológico de modelización con una validación preliminar sobre datos de rugby a 6 (ilustración adicional con baloncesto).
population: Datos de rugby a 6 de varios clubes franceses (tamaño muestral no indicado en el abstract).
method: Cada ataque se representa como un camino dirigido con información espacial absoluta y relativa centrada en el portador del balón, temporal y semántica. Con ese modelo se contrastan dos hipótesis: la pedagogía aplicada por el entrenador y la posición inicial de la defensa.
results: Los resultados preliminares indican efectos apreciables de ambas restricciones, sin cifras en el abstract.
conclusions: El modelo permite describir patrones tácticos como fenómenos emergentes y podría extenderse a otros deportes y a patrones de coordinación del equipo.
limitations: Resultados preliminares, muestra no detallada y validación en un solo deporte; no he podido leer el texto completo.
why: Une sistemas complejos y pedagogía (con Seifert entre los autores) y ofrece una forma de cuantificar cómo cambian las jugadas al variar restricciones y enfoque del entrenador.
practice: Puedes imitar la idea al registrar tus ataques: anota posición relativa al portador y orden temporal, y compara jugadas bajo distintas restricciones de tarea.
summary: Modelo de grafos que describe cada ataque con información espacial, temporal y semántica y lo aplica a rugby a 6 para ver el efecto de la pedagogía del entrenador y de la posición defensiva inicial. Los resultados son preliminares pero apuntan a efectos de ambas restricciones.

title: Training load and postexercise biochemical markers during small-sided games with and without a floater in U-18 soccer players
venue: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: Background Floaters may modify the demands of small-sided games (SSGs), but associated postexercise biochemical responses remain unclear. This exploratory study compared training load and postexercise biochemical markers between 4v4 SSG configurations with and without an in-field floater in U-18 soccer players. Methods Eight outfield players participated in a repeated-measures, within-subject study comprising four experimental sessions of 4v4 SSGs with goalkeepers, performed with or without an in-field floater (two sessions per condition). External load was assessed using global navigation satellite system and inertial-sensor measures, and internal load using heart rate and rating of perceived exertion (RPE). Blood samples were collected during postexercise recovery for lactate, interleukin-6 (IL-6), myoglobin, and cortisol analyses. Participant-level condition means were compared using paired t tests (n = 8), with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Exact paired sign-flip permutation tests were performed as sensitivity analyses. Results No external-load outcomes showed statistically significant between-condition differences after FDR correction (all adjusted p ≥ 0.188). Peak heart rate was lower in the configuration with a floater (mean difference, -9.00 bpm; 95% confidence interval [CI], -15.20 to -2.80; adjusted p = 0.038). Post-SSG blood lactate was also lower (-1.28 mmol/L; 95% CI, -1.90 to -0.66; adjusted p = 0.013), although this difference was substantially influenced by session-specific variability in an exploratory sensitivity analysis. Mean heart rate was also lower (-7.19 bpm; 95% CI, -14.11 to -0.27), but the difference was not statistically significant after FDR correction (adjusted p = 0.102). objective: Comparar carga de entrenamiento y marcadores bioquímicos post-ejercicio entre juegos 4v4 con y sin un comodín (floater) interior.
design: Estudio exploratorio intrasujeto de medidas repetidas, 4 sesiones (2 por condición) con secuencia de condiciones fija.
population: 8 jugadores de campo sub-18 de fútbol (Corea del Sur).
method: 4v4 con porteros, con o sin comodín. Carga externa con GNSS e inerciales, interna con FC y RPE; lactato, IL-6, mioglobina y cortisol tras el juego. t pareadas con corrección FDR y permutaciones como sensibilidad.
results: Sin diferencias en carga externa tras FDR (p ajustada ≥ 0,188). Con comodín, FC máxima −9 bpm (IC95% −15,2 a −2,8; p aj. 0,038) y lactato −1,28 mmol/L (p aj. 0,013), pero esto no se sostuvo en las permutaciones (p aj. 0,055–0,128). Sin diferencias en RPE, IL-6, mioglobina ni cortisol.
conclusions: La configuración del juego podría asociarse a la FC máxima; el lactato dependió mucho de la variabilidad entre sesiones.
limitations: n = 8, secuencia fija y cambio simultáneo del área relativa de juego: no permite atribuir causalidad al comodín.
why: Muestra que añadir un comodín (restricción de números) apenas cambia la carga externa, útil si diseñas juegos reducidos y quieres separar el efecto táctico del físico.
practice: Puedes usar el comodín para dar superioridad y aliviar la intensidad sin perder la carga externa, vigilando el espacio por jugador.
summary: En 4v4 sub-18, el comodín no modificó la carga externa y se asoció a menor FC máxima y lactato, aunque con una muestra de 8 y un diseño sin contrabalanceo los resultados son frágiles.

title: With or Without a Goalkeeper: Visual Strategies and Performance in Soccer Penalty Kicks
abstract: This study investigated how goalkeeper presence and behavior influenced visual attention, oculomotor responses, and penalty performance in soccer players of different expertise levels. Twenty male players (amateur: n = 9; elite: n = 11) each performed twenty-four penalty kicks under four different conditions: no goalkeeper (C1), a moving goalkeeper naive to shot direction (C2), a moving goalkeeper informed of shot direction (C3), and a stationary goalkeeper positioned centrally without attempting to save (C4). Eye movements were recorded using an eye tracker to measure fixation duration, the count, and pupil size across successful and unsuccessful kicks for all conditions. A mixed-design ANOVA revealed significant main effects of the goalkeeper condition (p < 0.001), the area of interest (p < 0.001), and the group (p < 0.05) on fixation duration, as well as a significant condition × group interaction (p < 0.01). Elite players exhibited longer fixation duration and distinct fixation-count patterns compared with amateurs, especially under goalkeeper-present conditions (C2–C4), reflecting superior attentional stability and cognitive efficiency. Pupil size was significantly larger in goalkeeper-present conditions than in the no-goalkeeper condition (p < 0.05); however, pupil size remained consistent across groups. Moreover, unsuccessful kicks were associated with greater pupil dilation and, in specific comparisons, longer fixation duration, indicating greater attentional demands. A significant three-way interaction (group × condition × direction, p < 0.05) demonstrated that visual strategies and performance outcomes were dynamically shaped by contextual constraints and the skill level. objective: Analizar cómo la presencia y el comportamiento del portero afectan a la atención visual, la respuesta oculomotora y el rendimiento en penaltis según la pericia.
design: Experimental transversal con diseño mixto (condición × grupo).
population: 20 futbolistas varones: 9 aficionados y 11 de élite.
method: 24 penaltis por jugador en 4 condiciones: sin portero, portero móvil sin información, portero informado de la dirección y portero central estático. Eye-tracker (fijaciones, duración, pupila) y ANOVA mixto.
results: Efectos principales de condición, zona de interés (p < 0,001) y grupo (p < 0,05) y una interacción condición × grupo (p < 0,01) en duración de fijación. Los de élite fijaron más tiempo con portero presente; la pupila fue mayor con portero y en los fallos.
conclusions: La pericia se asocia con mayor estabilidad atencional; el portero aumenta la demanda cognitiva.
limitations: Muestra pequeña, solo varones y tarea de laboratorio con baja representatividad; no he leído el texto completo.
why: Aporta datos sobre acoplamiento percepción-acción y la importancia de mantener al portero real en la tarea (representatividad).
practice: Entrena los penaltis con portero presente y variable en lugar de a portería vacía.
summary: Con eye-tracking, los futbolistas de élite mantienen fijaciones más estables que los aficionados en penaltis con portero; sin portero cambia el patrón visual, de modo que conviene diseñar la práctica con portero.

title: Numerical Relations and Skill Level Constrain Co-Adaptive Behaviors of Agents in Sports Teams
abstract: Similar to other complex systems in nature (e.g., a hunting pack, flocks of birds), sports teams have been modeled as social neurobiological systems in which interpersonal coordination tendencies of agents underpin team swarming behaviors. Swarming is seen as the result of agent co-adaptation to ecological constraints of performance environments by collectively perceiving specific possibilities for action (affordances for self and shared affordances). A major principle of invasion team sports assumed to promote effective performance is to outnumber the opposition (creation of numerical overloads) during different performance phases (attack and defense) in spatial regions adjacent to the ball. Such performance principles are assimilated by system agents through manipulation of numerical relations between teams during training in order to create artificially asymmetrical performance contexts to simulate overloaded and underloaded situations. Here we evaluated effects of different numerical relations differentiated by agent skill level, examining emergent inter-individual, intra- and inter-team coordination. Groups of association football players (national--NLP and regional-level--RLP) participated in small-sided and conditioned games in which numerical relations between system agents were manipulated (5v5, 5v4 and 5v3). Typical grouping tendencies in sports teams (major ranges, stretch indices, distances of team centers to goals and distances between the teams' opposing line-forces in specific team sectors) were recorded by plotting positional coordinates of individual agents through continuous GPS tracking. objective: Ver cómo las relaciones numéricas (5v5, 5v4, 5v3) y el nivel de habilidad condicionan la coordinación interindividual, intra e interequipo.
design: Cuasi-experimental transversal con tres juegos reducidos condicionados por grupo de nivel.
population: Jugadores de fútbol de nivel nacional (NLP, incluyendo internacionales sub-19) y regional (RLP, 17,9 ± 0,3 años, 9 ± 1,9 años de experiencia); 5 por equipo (Portugal).
method: Juegos 5v5, 5v4 y 5v3 con portero en campo de 47,3 × 30,6 m, 6 min por partido. Posiciones con GPS y variables colectivas: rangos de movimiento, índice de estiramiento y distancias de centroides y líneas. ANOVA.
results: La asimetría numérica modificó las regiones dominantes, la compacidad del equipo en inferioridad y las distancias entre líneas. El nivel de habilidad tuvo un efecto grande, por ejemplo mayor índice de estiramiento en NLP (8,58 vs 7,00; η² = 0,12) y en el equipo en inferioridad (7,99 vs RLP; η² = 0,16).
conclusions: Los equipos se coadaptan a las restricciones numéricas, y el diseño de tareas debe ajustarse al nivel de los jugadores.
limitations: Pocos jugadores por equipo, una sola sesión por condición y acceso restringido a los datos.
why: Es un trabajo clave de la dinámica ecológica aplicada a juegos reducidos: respalda manipular las relaciones numéricas como restricción de tarea.
practice: Puedes usar 5v4 o 5v3 para generar espacios y reajustes de líneas, adaptando la desigualdad al nivel del grupo.
summary: Tres juegos condicionados con GPS muestran que la desigualdad numérica y el nivel de habilidad reorganizan las distancias y la compacidad del equipo.
why_background: Es un estudio base sobre coadaptación y manipulación de números en juegos reducidos que sigue citándose en la literatura actual.

title: Football, Culture, Skill Development and Sport Coaching: Extending Ecological Approaches in Athlete Development Using the Skilled Intentionality Framework
abstract: In this manuscript, we extend ecological approaches and suggest ideas for enhancing athlete development by utilizing the Skilled Intentionality Framework. A broad aim is to illustrate the extent to which social, cultural and historical aspects of life are embodied in the way football is played and the skills young footballers develop during learning. Here, we contend that certain aspects of the world (i.e., environmental properties) are "weighted" with social and cultural significance, "standing out" to be more readily perceived and simultaneously acted upon when playing football. To comprehend how patterns of team coordination and athletic skill embody aspects of culture and context we outline the value-directedness of player-environment intentionality. We demonstrate that the values an individual can express are constrained by the character of the social institutions (i.e., football clubs) and the social order (i.e., form of life) in which people live. In particular, we illuminate the extent to which value-directedness can act as a constraint on the skill development of football players "for good or ill." We achieve this goal by outlining key ecological and relational concepts that help illustrate the extent to which affordances are value-realizing and intentionality is value-directed (exemplified, by footballers performing in a rondo). To enhance coaching practice, we offer: (a) insights into markers of skilled intentionality, and (b), the language of skilled intentions, as well as highlighting (c), an additional principle of Non-linear Pedagogy: Shaping skilled intentions, or more precisely shaping the value-directedness of player-environment intentionality. objective: Extender los enfoques ecológicos al desarrollo de futbolistas con el marco de intencionalidad hábil (Skilled Intentionality Framework).
design: Artículo teórico/conceptual con ejemplo ilustrativo (rondo).
population: No aplica.
method: Argumentación conceptual sobre afordancias cargadas de valor sociocultural y la intencionalidad dirigida por valores, ilustrada con un rondo.
results: No hay datos empíricos; propone marcadores y un lenguaje de intenciones hábiles para la práctica de entrenamiento.
conclusions: Las afordancias y la intencionalidad están orientadas por valores que el club y la cultura restringen para bien o para mal.
limitations: Propuesta teórica sin validación empírica.
why: Conecta dinámica ecológica con la cultura del club y el rol del entrenador en el desarrollo del talento.
practice: Te sirve para observar y nombrar intenciones de los jugadores durante rondos y juegos de posesión.
summary: Propone el marco de intencionalidad hábil para entender cómo la cultura y los valores moldean las habilidades de los futbolistas.
why_background: Marco teórico reciente que amplía la dinámica ecológica a la dimensión social del entrenamiento.

title: Metastable attunement and real-life skilled behavior
abstract: In everyday situations, and particularly in some sport and working contexts, humans face an inherently unpredictable and uncertain environment. All sorts of unpredictable and unexpected things happen but typically people are able to skillfully adapt. In this paper, we address two key questions in cognitive science. First, how is an agent able to bring its previously learned skill to bear on a novel situation? Second, how can an agent be both sensitive to the particularity of a given situation, while remaining flexibly poised for many other possibilities for action? We will argue that both the sensitivity to novel situations and the sensitivity to a multiplicity of action possibilities are enabled by the property of skilled agency that we will call metastable attunement. We characterize a skilled agent's flexible interactions with a dynamically changing environment in terms of metastable dynamics in agent-environment systems. What we find in metastability is the realization of two competing tendencies: the tendency of the agent to express their intrinsic dynamics and the tendency to search for new possibilities. Metastably attuned agents are ready to engage with a multiplicity of affordances, allowing for a balance between stability and flexibility. On the one hand, agents are able to exploit affordances they are attuned to, while at the same time being ready to flexibly explore for other affordances. Metastable attunement allows agents to smoothly transition between these possible configurations so as to adapt their behaviour to what the particular situation requires. We go on to describe the role metastability plays in learning of new skills, and in skilful behaviour more generally. design: Artículo teórico.
population: No aplica.
method: Introduce la «afinación metaestable» a partir de la dinámica metaestable de los sistemas agente-entorno.
results: Sin datos; define el equilibrio entre estabilidad y flexibilidad.
conclusions: Los agentes metaestables explotan afordancias conocidas y exploran otras nuevas.
limitations: Teórico, sin contraste empírico directo.
why: Aporta base conceptual a la variabilidad útil y la adaptabilidad en el aprendizaje.
practice: Justifica tareas con variabilidad que mantengan al jugador explorando.
summary: La afinación metaestable describe el equilibrio entre explotar afordancias y explorar otras nuevas en habilidades reales.
why_background: Sustenta los estudios actuales sobre adaptabilidad y metaestabilidad.

title: Is futsal a donor sport for football?: exploiting complementarity for early diversification in talent development
abstract: Introduction: In team sports like football, athlete development emerges through the continuous experience and practice of varied activities under variations in task and environmental constraints. Such variations in environmental and task constraints provide variable practice opportunities and experiences that promote an enrichment of the learning process through enhanced transfer, and the discovery of individual capabilities through diverse, functional play activities. Objectives: In this commentary, we discuss theoretical insights that suggest how the sport of futsal can provide a useful basis for supporting the transfer of skills to performance in association football. Conclusions: The complementary nature of the two sports can be exploited for skill acquisition in early diversification through emphasising selected performance–based affordances, behavioral correspondence between sports, and self-evident advances towards task goals. By taking up futsal at an early stage, future football players will have the opportunity to explore futsal tactical behaviors that will enrich their developing perceptual-motor landscape. Practial Implications: To ensure a complementary transfer of capabilities between the sports, coaching interventions should highlight informational constraints to improve the coupling of perception and action in players in futsal and association football and promote the utilization of relevant affordances available in practice task designs.
objective: Argumentar cómo el fútbol sala puede apoyar la transferencia de habilidades al fútbol en la diversificación temprana.
design: Comentario teórico.
population: No aplica.
method: Argumentación basada en restricciones, afordancias y correspondencia conductual.
results: Sin datos empíricos.
conclusions: Ambos deportes son complementarios y el fútbol sala enriquece el paisaje perceptivo-motor del futbolista.
limitations: No tiene evidencia empírica propia.
why: Útil para tu línea de talento y diversificación.
practice: Introduce tareas o sesiones de fútbol sala resaltando restricciones informacionales.
summary: El fútbol sala puede ser deporte donante del fútbol si se resaltan afordancias y correspondencia conductual.
why_background: Marco para la diversificación temprana vigente en la formación de jugadores.

title: Amplifying the effects of adding extra players during association football game-based scenarios
abstract: This study aimed to compare under-18 association football players' performance (age = 17.7±1.0 years; playing experience = 9.0 ± 3.2 years) when manipulating the number of teammates and opponents during football game-based practices. Time-motion, individual and tactical-related variables were monitored when manipulating conditions with different number of teammates and opponents (11vs11, No-Sup, No-Inf; 11vs12, Low-Sup, Low-Inf; 11vs13, Mod-Sup, Mod-Inf; and 11vs14, High-Sup, High-Inf). Results showed that adding teammates promoted increases in the longitudinal synchronization from No-Sup to Mod-Sup (Cohen's d with 95% of confidence intervals: 0.25 [0.12; 0.39]; p < .001) and High-Sup (0.61 [0.41; 0.82]; p < .001), while decreases in the distance to the nearest teammate, both in the offensive and defensive phases (p < .001 and p = .005, respectively). In addition, it was observed lower distance covered while running when playing in High-Sup compared to No-Sup (0.30 [-0.01; 0.61]; p = .002) during the defensive phase. Attacking in numerical inferiority promoted a higher variability in the distance to the nearest teammate from No-Inf to High-Inf (0.83 [0.27; 1.38]; p = .044), while decreasing the physical demands, specifically distance covered while running (-0.49 [-0.99; 0.01]; p = .039). In turn, defending, mainly in high-inferiority, increased the total distance covered compared to No-Inf (0.61 [0.30; 0.91]; p < .001) and led to a decrease in the distance to the nearest teammate (-0.90 [-1.35; -0.44]; p = .002). Overall, coaches may manipulate the number of teammates and opponents to promote distinct effects at the level of cooperation and opposition dynamical interactions.
objective: Ver cómo cambian la sincronización, las distancias entre compañeros/rivales y las exigencias físicas al añadir jugadores a un equipo (superioridad) o al rival (inferioridad) en juegos de fútbol 11 contra 11.
design: Cuasi-experimental transversal con cuatro condiciones de superioridad y cuatro de inferioridad numérica (11v11, 11v12, 11v13, 11v14).
population: 20 futbolistas sub-18 de un mismo equipo (17,7 ± 1,0 años; 9,0 ± 3,2 años de experiencia), nivel regional, Portugal; porteros excluidos.
method: Posicionamiento GPS y vídeo para medir sincronización longitudinal/lateral por díadas, distancia al compañero y rival más cercanos, su variabilidad y distancia recorrida corriendo, en fase ofensiva y defensiva. Modelos mixtos y tamaños del efecto (d de Cohen).
results: Añadir compañeros subió la sincronización longitudinal (d 0,25 hasta 0,61) y acercó a los jugadores entre sí; con 4 de más corrían menos en defensa. Atacar en inferioridad alta aumentó la variabilidad de la distancia al compañero (d 0,83) y bajó la carga física; defender en inferioridad alta elevó la distancia total (d 0,61).
conclusions: Variar el número de compañeros y rivales modifica la dinámica de cooperación y oposición, así que el entrenador puede usarlo como restricción de diseño de tarea.
limitations: Un solo equipo, sin porteros y con jugadores extra en posiciones fijas por condición; escenarios menos representativos de la competición.
why: Es un ejemplo claro de restricción numérica leída desde la dinámica ecológica y la coordinación colectiva, justo tu línea de sistemas complejos aplicados al fútbol.
practice: Para cambiar el comportamiento colectivo sin cambiar el campo, prueba 11v12 o 11v13 con comodines en una posición concreta y observa distancias entre líneas y ritmo de ataque.
summary: Estudio con GPS en 20 sub-18 que compara superioridades e inferioridades numéricas en juego 11v11 ampliado. La superioridad aumenta la sincronización y reduce distancias entre compañeros; la inferioridad ataca con más variabilidad y defiende con más desplazamiento. Estudio sólido para justificar manipulaciones numéricas como restricciones.
why_background: Estudio clave de manipulación numérica en juegos grandes, que se sigue citando en juegos reducidos y diseño de tareas.

title: Informing the Coaching Pedagogy of Game Modification in a Game Sense Approach with Affordance Theory
venue: Ágora/Ágora para la educación física y el deporte
abstract: The Game Sense coaching approach is founded on expectations of game-based practice as the game (or game form) becomes the focus and starting point of practice. The theory of affordances, a conceptual pillar of ecological modelling of perception and action in sport leading to a constraintsled game design perspective, provides a basis for understanding the modifying and adapting games as a pedagogical emphasis of the Game Sense approach. We review affordance theory leading to a demonstrated application of constraints-led learning in Touch Football. We conclude with the proposition of constraints-led game design as a logical semantics for the game-based practice assumptions of the Game Sense approach. This paper demonstrates the potential of affordance theory as a means of analysis of the task dynamics of Touch Football to inform a Game Sense coaching perspective for the sport.
objective: Proponer la teoría de affordances y el diseño de juegos basado en restricciones como base conceptual del enfoque Game Sense en coaching.
design: Artículo teórico con ejemplo aplicado (plan de sesión en Touch Football).
population: No aplica.
method: Revisa la teoría de affordances y el modelo ecológico de percepción-acción, y contrasta un plan de sesión Game Sense (juegos 3v3 modificados, parada para análisis) con un plan técnico (rondas de carrera y pases sin oposición). Ilustra cuatro vías de modificar el juego: área, equipamiento, tarea y reglas.
results: No hay datos empíricos; el resultado es un marco: modificar juegos equivale a manipular restricciones que cambian qué acciones el entorno ofrece al jugador.
conclusions: El diseño de juegos con restricciones es la semántica lógica de los supuestos del Game Sense, y las affordances permiten analizar la dinámica de la tarea.
limitations: Es conceptual, sin evaluación empírica ni muestra; el ejemplo es de Touch Football.
why: Conecta el Game Sense que se usa en la práctica con el marco CLA/dinámica ecológica, útil para fundamentar teóricamente tus sesiones.
practice: Usa las cuatro palancas (área, material, tarea, reglas) como lista de comprobación al modificar un juego reducido y pregúntate qué affordance quieres que emerja.
summary: Trabajo teórico que vincula Game Sense, affordances y diseño de juegos con restricciones, con un ejemplo en Touch Football. Aporta un lenguaje común para justificar modificaciones de juego en el entrenamiento.
why_background: Base teórica en abierto que enlaza la pedagogía de juegos modificados con la teoría de affordances.

title: Developing skill within the context of a Game-Based Approach
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Limited research has examined continued skill development in adult high-performance sport. In addition, while game-based approaches emphasise the concurrent development of technical excellence and tactical nous, there is a lack of clarity in relation to how coaches develop skill within a games-based approach. As such, this paper explored coaches’ understanding of skill and their approaches to the development of skill within high-performance cohorts through a game-based approach. Individual, semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight coaches with experience coaching at the highest level of Gaelic football; these coaches self-identified as adhering to a game-based approach, albeit not to a particular framework. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied to the resulting transcripts. The analysis identified two key challenges coaches faced in relation to skill development through a game-based approach: competing priorities for coaches in relation to team preparation within training sessions, compounded by competing priorities for players in terms of athletic development outside of training sessions. Despite these competing priorities, the coaches endorsed skill development as an important function of the high-performance coach and reported a sophisticated definition of skill. The coaches described a variety of activities which were used to support players’ development of skill, consistent with their espoused games-based approach to coaching. However, more sophisticated game design, better integration of unopposed activities and games, developing player self-regulatory skills and enhanced coherence between coaches appear to be ways in which skill development could be enhanced to address the challenges coaches identified and maximise the benefits of employing a game-b
summary: Entrevistas a 8 entrenadores de élite de fútbol gaélico sobre cómo desarrollan la habilidad con un enfoque basado en juegos; señalan prioridades enfrentadas y piden mejor diseño de juegos y autorregulación del jugador.

title: Critical application of TGfU in sports coaching
abstract: Background The foundational nature of the ‘Teaching Games for Understanding’ (TGfU) approach [Thorpe, R., D. Bunker, and L. Almond. 1986. Rethinking games teaching. Loughborough: University of Technology.] has led to considerable interest from researchers and practitioners since its inception [Stolz, S., and S. Pill. 2014. “Teaching Games and Sport for Understanding.” European Physical Education Review 20 (1): 36–71. https://doi.org/10.1177/1356336X13496001]. Consequently, many variations of TGfU have come to the fore [Mitchell, S., J. Oslin, and L. Griffin. 2020. Teaching sport concepts and skills: A tactical games approach. 4th ed. Champaign, IL: Human Kinetics.]. Despite the considerable interest from physical education related researchers, those in sports coaching have been slower to embrace the TGfU approach, particularly in competitive adult settings [Kinnerk, S., S. Harvey, C. MacDonncha, and M. Lyons. 2018. “A Review of the Game-Based Approaches to Coaching Literature in Competitive Team Sport Settings.” Quest.]. Indeed, there is a lack of consensus about the TGfU’s efficiency and studies have shown that practitioners lack knowledge on how to implement it in their own context [Karagiannis, K., and S. Pill. 2017. “A Case Study Exploring Coaching Practice and Coaching Perspectives at One Soccer (Football) Club.” Scientific Journal of Education, Sports, and Health 18 (1): 140–150.].Purpose Therefore, the aim of this study was to critically explore the utility of TGfU as a pedagogical approach within a competitive sports coaching setting, whilst considering its impact on the coach and players’ learning.Methodology An Action Research (AR) methodology involving progressive cycles of practice over the course of a full eight-month volleyball season. summary: Investigación-acción durante una temporada de voleibol (8 meses) que explora la utilidad del TGfU en entrenamiento competitivo adulto y su impacto en el aprendizaje de entrenador y jugadores.

title: Metabolic, Endocrine, and Neurotrophic Responses to a 4v4 Small-Sided Game Following Brief Music or Mindfulness After a Mental-Fatigue Exposure: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Prolonged cognitive load, including short-form social-media use, may influence soccer-specific performance, yet the perceptual, metabolic, endocrine and neurotrophic effects of brief post-fatigue strategies such as music and mindfulness remain unclear. This study compared 15 min music, 15 min mindfulness (body scan) and time-matched control after a 45 min short-form social-media mental-fatigue exposure. Methods: Sixteen trained male soccer players completed a randomized, counterbalanced, repeated-measures crossover trial. Each session comprised the exposure, condition, a standardized warm-up and a 4v4 small-sided game (SSG). Venous blood was obtained pre-protocol (T1) and approximately 5 min post-SSG (T2) for serum lactate, cortisol and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Perceptual and technical-performance outcomes were also analysed using linear mixed-effects models. Results: Post-condition mental-effort scores differed by condition (F(2,30) = 12.117, p < 0.001) and were lower in music and mindfulness than in control in a time-point-specific model, although baseline mental effort also differed between conditions; perceived mental fatigue, post-SSG exertion and enjoyment did not differ. Condition effects emerged for successful passes (p = 0.020), ball recoveries (p = 0.010) and ball losses (p = 0.018), all highest during mindfulness; pass success percentage, shot outcomes and net ball recovery were unchanged. Overall lactate (p = 0.013) and cortisol (p = 0.047) differed between selected conditions when averaged across sampling times, possibly reflecting pre-existing differences, but BDNF did not differ (p = 0.559), and no time effects or condition × time interactions were observed. summary: Cruzado aleatorizado en 16 futbolistas: tras 45 min de redes sociales, música o mindfulness 15 min antes de un 4v4; hubo más pases acertados y recuperaciones tras mindfulness, sin cambios en BDNF.

title: Evaluating Passing Performance in Youth Football: A Systematic Review Toward an Ecological Dynamics Framework
venue: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
abstract: Passing is a fundamental component of football performance, yet current approaches to evaluating passing performance in youth football remain methodologically diverse and conceptually fragmented. This systematic review aimed to map and critically evaluate existing approaches to evaluating passing performance in youth football, focusing on evaluation dimensions, indicators, tools, scenarios, and the extent to which individual, task, and environmental constraints are reported or incorporated. The review also aimed to synthesize the evidence toward a conceptual micro-meso-macro framework for representative passing evaluation. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus was conducted for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2000 and September 2025 involving youth association football players aged 19 years or younger and reporting passing-related outcomes. Studies were selected according to predefined eligibility criteria and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methodological and reporting quality was assessed using a 16-item checklist, and included studies were coded using an individual-task-environment constraint framework. The review protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework before database searching, screening, data extraction, ecological coding, and synthesis (OSF registration ID: 2bqfy). Thirty-six studies were included. The reviewed approaches were organized into three analytical dimensions: individual technical ability, contextual decision-making ability, and passing team contribution. Contextual decision-making represented the largest group of studies, whereas team contribution approaches were less frequently represented. The evidence map suggested an overall imbalance toward controlled and sta
objective: Mapear cómo se evalúa el pase en fútbol de formación y hasta qué punto esas evaluaciones incorporan restricciones del individuo, la tarea y el entorno.
design: Revisión sistemática PRISMA 2020 preregistrada en OSF (2000–sep 2025; PubMed, WoS, Scopus), con codificación ecológica de restricciones y propuesta de marco conceptual micro-meso-macro.
population: 36 estudios con futbolistas ≤19 años; el sexo consta en 21 (58,3 %), el nivel competitivo en 35, la maduración biológica solo en 4 (11,1 %) y la posición en 17.
method: Evaluaron la calidad con una lista de 16 ítems y clasificaron las evaluaciones en habilidad técnica individual, toma de decisión contextual y aportación del jugador al equipo, según herramienta, indicador y escenario (cerrado, juego reducido o partido).
results: Predominan las evaluaciones controladas y estandarizadas (tests cerrados, Footbonaut, sistemas de luces); la toma de decisión contextual es el bloque más numeroso y la aportación al equipo (redes de pase) el menos. Los juegos reducidos y el análisis de partido se usan poco y el reporte de variables de los participantes es muy desigual.
conclusions: El control metodológico pesa más que la representatividad ecológica; proponen un marco micro-meso-macro que trata el pase como propiedad emergente de restricciones que interactúan, sin validarlo todavía.
limitations: Solo artículos en inglés y tres bases, sin metaanálisis por heterogeneidad, y el sistema de codificación es propio y no está validado.
why: Es tu marco (dinámica ecológica y diseño representativo) aplicado a cómo se mide el pase en cantera, con un mapa claro de huecos de investigación.
practice: Complementa los tests cerrados de pase con juegos reducidos y situaciones de partido donde registres éxito bajo presión, uso de líneas de pase y retención de balón.
summary: Revisión de 36 estudios que muestra que la evaluación del pase juvenil prioriza tests controlados frente a contextos representativos. Propone un marco micro-meso-macro para evaluar el pase con restricciones ecológicas. Es una síntesis conceptual, aún sin validar.

title: Impacto de la metodología no lineal sobre variables técnicas y cinemáticas en el entrenamiento de fútbol
venue: Journal of Sport and Health Research
objective: Comparar una tarea de metodología no lineal con otra analítica tradicional en variables técnicas y cinemáticas.
design: Cuasi-experimental transversal con dos tareas de 8 minutos en el mismo espacio (40×40 m), observadas 8 veces a lo largo de 3 semanas.
population: 22 futbolistas semiprofesionales masculinos (21,2 ± 1,9 años, 12 años de experiencia).
method: GPS a 10 Hz (distancias por rangos de velocidad, aceleraciones, tiempo de participación), RPE y codificación por vídeo de pase, control y tiro por dos entrenadores UEFA Pro; comparación con t de Student.
results: La tarea no lineal dio más tiempo de participación (7,21 vs 3,87 min), más distancia total (389 vs 194 m), más aceleraciones (28 vs 15) y mayor RPE (7,2 vs 4,4); no hubo diferencias en >22,3 km/h ni en deceleraciones. En técnica, la tarea analítica registró más pases totales (146 vs 105; p = 0,048), mientras la no lineal tuvo más pases de exterior (11,9 vs 4,2).
conclusions: Los autores concluyen que la metodología no lineal favorece más las variables técnicas y cinemáticas y ofrece vivencias más ricas. Ojo: sus propios datos de pase no apoyan del todo esa conclusión.
limitations: Sesiones breves, muestra pequeña, tareas no equiparables en carga y sin medidas de calidad o transferencia al juego.
why: Es un estudio en español de pedagogía no lineal en fútbol; te sirve como ejemplo de lo que se publica y de sus límites, porque el resumen sobrevende los resultados.
practice: Si usas tareas no lineales para elevar la implicación y la carga, ten en cuenta que más participación no implica más pases ni mejor ejecución: registra calidad, no solo volumen.
summary: Compara dos tareas de 8 min en 22 jugadores semiprofesionales: la no lineal duplica participación y distancia, pero genera menos pases totales que la analítica. La conclusión de los autores es más favorable que sus tablas.

title: Framework and consensus statement for the implementation of sided game training in football (soccer)
venue: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
objective: Crear un marco unificado y recomendaciones basadas en evidencia para diseñar, monitorizar y aplicar juegos reducidos (sided games) en fútbol.
design: Declaración de consenso en tres fases: modelo teórico, umbrella review de 12 revisiones y metaanálisis, y votación ciega en escala de 9 puntos (consenso 7–9).
population: Panel multidisciplinar de unos 20 expertos internacionales (n exacto no confirmado); no aplica a jugadores.
method: Definieron prioridades a partir de la umbrella review y redactaron las declaraciones de forma iterativa hasta votarlas.
results: Siete declaraciones alcanzaron consenso: definición de juego reducido, factores que influyen (filosofía del entrenador y restricciones de entorno, tarea e individuo), principios de monitorización, y beneficios y límites. Son eficaces para capacidad aeróbica y comportamiento táctico-técnico, y menos para fuerza, potencia y alta velocidad.
conclusions: Presentan el primer marco para el entrenamiento con juegos reducidos y señalan lagunas de investigación.
limitations: Consenso de expertos, no evidencia experimental; basado en revisiones previas.
why: Ordena la terminología de los juegos reducidos con las restricciones individuo-tarea-entorno de tu enfoque; sigue vigente como referencia compartida.
practice: Úsalo como lista de verificación al diseñar un juego reducido: qué restricciones manipulas y cómo monitorizas el efecto, sabiendo que no sirve para trabajar velocidad máxima.
summary: Marco de consenso con siete declaraciones sobre cómo definir, diseñar y monitorizar juegos reducidos en fútbol. Subraya las restricciones y los límites de la herramienta. Lo he valorado solo a partir del abstract y la ficha de la editorial.

title: Dynamics of tactical behaviour in association football when manipulating players' space of interaction
abstract: The analysis of positional data in association football allows the spatial distribution of players during matches to be described in order to improve the understanding of tactical-related constraints on the behavioural dynamics of players. The aim of this study was to identify how players' spatial restrictions affected the exploratory tactical behaviour and constrained the perceptual-motor workspace of players in possession of the ball, as well as inter-player passing interactions. Nineteen professional outfield male players were divided into two teams of 10 and 9 players, respectively. The game was played under three spatial constraints: a) players were not allowed to move out of their allocated zones, except for the player in possession of the ball; b) players were allowed to move to an adjacent zone, and; c) non-specific spatial constraints. Positional data was captured using a 5 Hz interpolated GPS tracking system and used to define the configuration states of players for each second in time. The configuration state comprised 37 categories derived from tactical actions, distance from the nearest opponent, distance from the target and movement speed. Notational analysis of players in possession of the ball allowed the mean time of ball possession and the probabilities of passing the ball between players to be calculated. The results revealed that the players' long-term exploratory behaviour decreased and their short-term exploration increased when restricting their space of interaction. Relaxing players' positional constraints seemed to increase the speed of ball flow dynamics. objective: Ver cómo las restricciones espaciales sobre los jugadores modifican la conducta táctica exploratoria y las interacciones de pase.
design: Experimental con tres condiciones de restricción espacial en juego de 10 vs 9.
population: 19 jugadores profesionales masculinos de campo.
method: Posiciones por GPS a 5 Hz, 37 estados de configuración por segundo (acciones tácticas, distancia al rival y a la meta, velocidad) y análisis notacional de posesión y probabilidades de pase.

conclusions: Las restricciones espaciales reconfiguran el espacio perceptivo-motor y las redes de pase.

summary: Tres condiciones de restricción espacial en jugadores profesionales muestran cambios en la exploración táctica y en los patrones de pase. Referencia muy citada (97 citas).

title: Collective states and their transitions in football
abstract: Movement, positioning and coordination of player formations is a key aspect for the performance of teams within field-based sports. The increased availability of player tracking data has given rise to numerous studies that focus on the relationship between simple descriptive statistics surrounding team formation and performance. While these existing approaches have provided a high-level a view of team-based spatial formations, there is limited research on the nature of collective movement across players within teams and the establishment of stable collective states within game play. This study draws inspiration from the analysis of collective movement in nature, such as that observed within schools of fish and flocking birds, to explore the existence of collective states within the phases of play in soccer. Order parameters and metrics describing group motion and shape are derived from player movement tracks to uncover the nature of the team's collective states and transitions. This represents a unique addition to the current body of work around the analysis of player movement in team sports. The results from this study demonstrate that sequences of ordered collective behaviours exist with relatively rapid transitions between highly aligned polar and un-ordered swarm behaviours (and vice-versa). Defensive phases of play have a higher proportion of ordered team movement than attacking phases, indicating that movements linked with attacking tactics, such as player dispersion to generate passing and shooting opportunities leads to lower overall collective order. Exploration within this study suggests that defensive tactics, such as reducing the depth or width to close passing opportunities, allows for higher team movement speeds and increased levels of collective order. title: Group Cohesion and Salivary Oxytocin During a Six-Month Coordination-Based Training Program in Junior Handball Players: A Prospective Non-Randomized Controlled Intervention Study.
abstract: Whether coordination-based training can develop group cohesion in youth sport, and how cohesion relates to peripheral oxytocin, is unclear. We examined cohesion and salivary oxytocin during a six-month coordination- and cohesion-oriented program in junior handball players. Sixty-four male players (12-14 years) from four clubs joined a prospective, non-randomized, within-club controlled study (not prospectively registered). In each club, one pre-existing training slot (eight players) formed the experimental group (EG; n = 32) and the other the control group (CG; n = 32). For 24 weeks (three sessions/week), EG replaced 20-25 min of technical-tactical work with coordination, cooperation, and interpersonal-synchrony exercises. The primary outcome was Youth Sport Environment Questionnaire (YSEQ) Task Cohesion. In the baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust analysis, T1 Task Cohesion was 0.72 points higher in EG than CG (95% CI 0.22-1.23; p = 0.010); Social Cohesion differed similarly (adjusted difference 0.77 points; 95% CI 0.33-1.22; p = 0.003). The adjusted oxytocin difference was imprecise and non-significant (5.0 pg/mL; 95% CI -0.01 to 10.02; p = 0.050), and oxytocin change was unrelated to Task Cohesion change. The program was accompanied by a more favorable cohesion trajectory than time-matched standard training. Non-randomized allocation precludes causal conclusions; oxytocin findings remain exploratory.
objective: Ver si seis meses de entrenamiento de coordinación y cohesión mejoran la cohesión de grupo y cómo se relaciona con la oxitocina salival.
design: Prospectivo, no aleatorizado, con grupo control dentro de cada club, 24 semanas × 3 sesiones; no preregistrado.
population: 64 jugadores de balonmano varones de 12–14 años de cuatro clubes (32 experimentales, 32 control).
method: El grupo experimental sustituyó 20–25 min de trabajo técnico-táctico por ejercicios de coordinación, cooperación y sincronía interpersonal; cohesión con el YSEQ y oxitocina salival.
results: La cohesión de tarea fue 0,72 puntos mayor en el grupo experimental (IC95 % 0,22–1,23; p = 0,010) y la social 0,77 (p = 0,003); la diferencia de oxitocina fue imprecisa y no significativa (p = 0,050).
conclusions: El programa se acompañó de mejor cohesión, aunque sin inferencia causal; lo de la oxitocina es exploratorio.
limitations: No aleatorizado ni preregistrado, y muestra pequeña de un solo deporte.
why: Conecta la coordinación interpersonal y la sincronía con la cohesión de equipo en jóvenes, un puente con los sistemas complejos.
practice: Puedes reservar 20 min por sesión para tareas de sincronía y cooperación sin balón o con balón.
summary: Seis meses de tareas de coordinación y sincronía se asociaron a mayor cohesión de tarea y social en balonmano juvenil. No es causal y la oxitocina no mostró relación.

title: Can Standardized Small-Sided Games Be Used as a Tool to Monitor Post-Match Fatigue in Male Academy Soccer Players?
abstract: This study aimed to analyze residual post-match fatigue using time-motion analysis across small-sided games (SSGs), fitness performance, and heart rate variability (HRV) in academy soccer players. Fifteen male academy players (18.3 ± 0.6 years) performed four SSG formats: 3 vs. 3 and 3 vs. 3 + 2 goalkeepers, played on small (25 × 18 m; 75 m2 per player) and large (36 × 25 m; 150 m2 per player) areas in a four-week experimental design. Two non-match weeks served as baseline weeks, and two weeks followed an official match. Time-motion during SSGs was monitored via GNSS. Before each training session (24, 72, and 120 h post-match), HRV, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, and maximum isometric force (MIF) of the hamstrings were measured. External load metrics were generally lower in post-match sessions than in non-match weeks; however, their low reliability limited the interpretability of SSG outputs. CMJ height was reduced, MIF was elevated post-match, whereas HRV showed distinct mid-week responses, decreasing in starters but increasing in non-starters. Post-match fatigue was evident in neuromuscular performance but was inconsistently reflected in SSG outputs. CMJ height reliably reflects post-match fatigue in male academy soccer players and should be prioritized when monitoring neuromuscular recovery.
objective: Valorar si los juegos reducidos estandarizados sirven para monitorizar la fatiga residual tras el partido.
design: Experimental de cuatro semanas (dos de referencia y dos tras partido oficial).
population: 15 futbolistas de cantera masculinos (18,3 ± 0,6 años).
method: Cuatro formatos de 3v3 (con o sin porteros, espacio de 75 o 150 m² por jugador) con GNSS, más HRV, CMJ y fuerza isométrica de isquios a 24, 72 y 120 h.
results: La carga externa fue menor tras partido, pero su baja fiabilidad limitó la interpretación; el CMJ bajó de forma fiable y la HRV varió según fueran titulares o no.
conclusions: La fatiga se ve en el rendimiento neuromuscular, no de forma consistente en los juegos reducidos; priorizar el CMJ.
limitations: Muestra de 15 y baja fiabilidad de las métricas de los juegos reducidos.
why: Pone a prueba el uso de juegos reducidos como herramienta de monitorización; te avisa de su baja fiabilidad.
practice: No uses un 3v3 para medir la fatiga; usa el CMJ.
summary: Los juegos reducidos 3v3 no reflejaron bien la fatiga postpartido, mientras el CMJ sí.

title: Neuromuscular Performance Thresholds to Support Player Development in a Professional Soccer Academy.
abstract: We aimed to compare neuromuscular performance between academy soccer players (U-17, U-19, and U-21 categories) and first-team players, and to establish neuromuscular performance thresholds associated with the first-team level. Ninety-four male players participated and were followed over two seasons. Neuromuscular performance was assessed using force-plate and force-sensing frame technologies, including isometric hip adduction and abduction, Nordic hamstring exercise, countermovement jump (CMJ), and isometric squat hold. Peak force, eccentric and concentric peak force, rate of force development, impulse, modified reactive strength index (RSI-modified), dynamic strength index (DSI) and limb asymmetry were analyzed. Linear mixed models, binary logistic generalized estimating equations (GEE), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed. The neuromuscular variables that best discriminated between soccer academy and first-team were maximal hip pull force (OR = 2.53, p < 0.001), concentric peak force (OR = 2.42, p < 0.001), eccentric peak force (OR = 1.31, p = 0.046), modified RSI (OR = 2.00, p < 0.001), RFD at 200 ms (OR = 1.46, p = 0.004), and DSI (OR = 2.13, p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified practical cutoff values for maximal hip abduction force (442 N), maximal concentric and eccentric forces during the CMJ (1856 and 1804 N, respectively), modified RSI (0.58 m·s-1) and DSI (0.57). First-team players demonstrate superior neuromuscular performance to academy players. The identified cutoff values should be considered exploratory benchmarks for distinguishing current competitive levels and require external, prospective validation in independent cohorts from other clubs before practical application.
objective: Comparar el rendimiento neuromuscular de la cantera con el primer equipo y fijar umbrales asociados al primer equipo.
design: Longitudinal de dos temporadas con modelos mixtos, GEE y curvas ROC.
population: 94 futbolistas masculinos de sub-17, sub-19, sub-21 y primer equipo de un club profesional.
method: Plataformas de fuerza y marco de fuerza: aducción y abducción isométricas de cadera, Nordic, CMJ y sentadilla isométrica.
results: Discriminaron mejor la fuerza máxima de cadera (OR 2,53), la fuerza concéntrica (OR 2,42), el RSI modificado (OR 2,00) y el DSI (OR 2,13); cortes: 442 N de abducción, 0,58 m·s-1 de RSI-mod y 0,57 de DSI.
conclusions: El primer equipo supera a la cantera; los cortes son referencias exploratorias.
limitations: Un solo club, sin validación externa prospectiva.
why: Es desarrollo del talento visto desde la condición física, con cuidado en no tratar los umbrales como criterio de selección.
practice: Usa los valores como referencia orientativa, nunca como filtro de selección.
summary: Umbrales neuromusculares que separan cantera y primer equipo en 94 jugadores; exploratorios y de un solo club.

title: To Ensure Peak Velocity in Soccer, Coaches Should Stimulate Players to Run.
abstract: The aim of this study was to compare the peak velocities reached by professional soccer players during multiple training tasks and friendly matches, taking into account players' positions. Global positioning system data were obtained from twenty-three soccer players (age: 24.8 ± 4.1 years; body height: 180.3 ± 6.3 cm; body mass: 75.7 ± 5.0 kg) who played for the same professional first division team of the Spanish league (La Liga). The peak of velocity (km•h-1) of ten different training tasks was analyzed according to the players' position. The results showed that there were significant differences (p tactical velocity task (TVE, n = 53), friendly match (FM, n = 231) > large-sided game (LSG, n = 146) > medium-sided game (MSG, n = 273) > evolution task (EVO, n = 381), high interval intensity training (HIIT, n = 227), small-sided game (SSG, n = 407) > large-sided ball-possession game (LSBPG, n = 227) > small-sided ball-possession game (SSBPG, n = 316) and, 2) that in the tasks with lower peak velocities (MSG, EVO, HIIT, SSG, LSBPG and SSBPG), no differences were found in their positions. Therefore, different training tasks create different peak velocity demands, and tasks with higher peak velocities and role-specificity (TVE, FM, LSG, and MSG) require different needs from players in different positions.
objective: Comparar la velocidad pico en diez tareas de entrenamiento y amistosos según la posición.
design: Observacional con GPS.
population: 23 jugadores profesionales de La Liga (24,8 ± 4,1 años).
method: Velocidad pico por tarea y posición.

title: A transformer-based multimodal fusion framework for ordinal motor skill-level assessment with biomechanical association analysis
abstract: Accurate motor skill assessment is essential for objective sports performance evaluation and data-driven coaching support. However, existing approaches often rely on single sensors, conventional classification models, or limited biomechanical interpretation, restricting their ability to capture comprehensive movement characteristics and ordered skill relationships. To address these limitations, this study proposes BioSkillFormer, a Transformer-based multimodal fusion framework for classifying badminton players into beginner, intermediate, and expert skill levels. The proposed framework integrates raw multimodal sensor sequences, timefrequency representations, biomechanical feature tokens, and reliability-aware cross-modal attention to capture complementary information from pose, electromyography (EMG), foot pressure, eye gaze, and video data. Skill-level prediction is formulated as an ordinal classification problem to preserve the natural progression of motor expertise. The framework was evaluated using the MultiSenseBadminton dataset under a subject-independent evaluation protocol. Experimental results demonstrated that BioSkillFormer achieved an accuracy of 0.8495, macro-F1 of 0.8375, balanced accuracy of 0.8420, ordinal mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.1560, and quadratic weighted kappa of 0.8530, outperforming single-sensor, timefrequency Transformer, and standard multimodal Transformer comparative methods. Ablation experiments indicated that ordinal loss, biomechanical tokens, timefrequency modeling, reliability-aware fusion, supervised contrastive learning, and masked modality reconstruction contributed to the observed performance. title: Gender Differences in Pre-Service Physical Education Teachers' Visual Behaviour: An Eye-Tracking Study.
abstract: (1) Background: Teachers' visual attention is central to professional vision, yet whether teacher gender influences gaze allocation in Physical Education remains unclear. This study examined gender-related differences in visual attentional deployment when teachers observed students' motor competence, behavioural engagement, off-task behaviour, and gender. (2) Methods: Sixty pre-service Physical Education teachers observed video-recorded tasks from a class while wearing Tobii Pro Glasses 3. Fixation metrics were quantified across predefined areas of interest and compared between teacher genders. (3) Results: Female and male teachers showed comparable total and mean fixation durations. However, the former produced significantly more fixations during the closed task towards on-task students and with higher motor competence. Female teachers also showed higher fixation frequency regardless of whether off-task behaviour was successfully identified, and made more fixations towards both female and male students during this task. These differences were not consistently observed during the open task. (4) Conclusions: Teacher gender differed primarily with fixation frequency rather than fixation duration, and this effect was context-dependent. Additionally, greater visual sampling did not necessarily correspond to more accurate behavioural noticing. Mobile eye-tracking can reveal gender-related and task-sensitive differences in teachers' visual behaviour, with potential applications in Physical Education teacher education and professional development.
summary: Eye-tracking en 60 docentes de EF en formación: las mujeres hicieron más fijaciones en la tarea cerrada, sin diferencias de duración.

title: Shooting accuracy and conditioning characteristics in proficient and non-proficient male perimeter basketball players: effects of distance and condition.
venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
abstract: Shooting accuracy is a key performance indicator in basketball, highlighting the importance of understanding how it varies with playing proficiency across different shooting conditions and distances. The present study had a three-fold aim to examine: i) the effects of shooting distance and condition complexity on shooting accuracy with respect to playing proficiency, ii) differences in shooting accuracy betwee playing proficient (PP) and non-proficient (NP) basketball perimeter players across different distances and conditions, and iii) differences in conditioning characteristics between PP and NP. The sample included 14 PP (age: 23.8 ± 3.4 years; body height: 189.4 ± 5.3 cm; body mass: 85.8 ± 5.6 kg) and 14 NP (age: 20.2 ± 2.0 years; body height: 182.7 ± 6.3 cm; body mass: 74.0 ± 10.2 kg) perimeter players. Three shooting conditions were assessed: stationary, dynamic, and competitive, across three distances (free-throw, two-point, and three-point). Conditioning characteristics were evaluated using a comprehensive battery of tests encompassing lower- and upper-body power, aerobic fitness, sprinting speed, change-of-direction speed, anaerobic capacity, and fatigue resistance. A binomial generalized linear mixed model examined all main effects and interactions. Independent-samples t-tests with Holm correction assessed differences in conditioning characteristics, quantified using Hedges' g. Even though PP showed greater overall shooting accuracy (p = .041), playing proficiency did not significantly moderate the effects of shooting condition or distance (all p ≥ .431). Accuracy declined with increasing distance and condition complexity (both p < .001), with a condition×distance interaction (p = .024). title: Reciprocal within-person associations between physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment among primary school students participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum: a four-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
abstract: Introduction Physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment are central to children’s motivation to be active, yet their temporal ordering and within-person interplay remain unclear. This study examined their reciprocal associations among 1,279 Chinese students in Grades 5 and 6 participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum. Methods General physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment were assessed on four occasions separated by 33, 28, and 28 days. Longitudinal measurement invariance was tested before conventional cross-lagged panel models and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were compared. The primary RI-CLPM used class-clustered robust maximum likelihood and full information maximum likelihood for missing data. Results Scalar invariance was supported for both measures, and temporal equality constraints were not rejected. At the between-person level, average self-efficacy and enjoyment were positively correlated, r = 0.672, p < 0.001. In the retained equal-lag model, higher-than-usual self-efficacy predicted subsequent higher-than-usual enjoyment, b = 0.147, 95% CI [0.096, 0.198], βs = 0.146–0.154, p < 0.001. Higher-than-usual enjoyment also predicted subsequent self-efficacy, b = 0.088, 95% CI [0.026, 0.150], βs = 0.083–0.084, p = 0.005. The directional contrast was not significant, p = 0.063. Both associations remained positive in the corresponding complete-case model (n = 1,025), after class-by-wave mean adjustment, and under the specified missing-data sensitivity scenarios. Discussion The findings support reciprocal within-person temporal associations between general physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment. title: Cooperative networks in team invasion games: A systematic mapping review
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Team invasion games are sports in which individual team members interact and exchange information to coordinate their behaviours and actions in pursuit of the common goal of winning matches. Researchers have used social network analysis to quantify the cooperative behaviours of sports teams (cooperative network analysis), yet this research exists across an array of disciplines and uses various methods. Therefore, accessibility for practitioners and researchers interested in using it to quantify team cooperation in team invasion games may be limited. This systematic mapping review aimed to identify, report and discuss research in this emerging research area. Articles were systematically searched in electronic databases and reference list scans resulting in 112 papers included. Football was the most studied sport ( n = 91), and passing was the most observed interaction between players within a sports team ( n = 107). This review further revealed a lack of consistency in reporting between the included studies with respect to nomenclature and network measures. A comprehensive map of the current literature on the use of cooperative network analysis in team invasion games is provided which can be used by practitioners and researchers tasked with or interested in analysing team performance.
objective: Mapear la investigación que usa análisis de redes cooperativas para cuantificar la cooperación en deportes de invasión.
design: Revisión sistemática de mapeo (systematic mapping review).
population: 112 artículos incluidos; el fútbol es el deporte más estudiado (n=91) y el pase la interacción más observada (n=107).
method: Búsqueda sistemática en bases electrónicas y revisión de referencias, con clasificación de deportes, interacciones y medidas de red empleadas.
results: Hay poca consistencia en la nomenclatura y en las medidas de red que se reportan entre estudios. Los autores ofrecen un mapa completo de la literatura.
conclusions: El campo es amplio pero heterogéneo; el mapa sirve de guía a investigadores y practicantes que quieran analizar cooperación en equipo.
limitations: Es un mapeo descriptivo: no valora la calidad de los estudios ni sintetiza efectos. Solo he podido leer el abstract.
why: Te da el panorama de cómo se estudia la coordinación entre jugadores desde la teoría de redes y qué medidas estandarizar si quieres hacerlo tú.
practice: Antes de montar un análisis de redes en tu equipo, elige medidas ya habituales (pases como aristas, densidad, centralidad) para poder comparar con la literatura.
summary: Mapa de 112 trabajos sobre redes de cooperación en deportes de invasión, con el fútbol y el pase como protagonistas y una notable falta de uniformidad en las métricas.

title: Social network analysis in football: a systematic review of performance and tactical applications
abstract: Introduction: This systematic review aims to critically examine the application of social network analysis (SNA) in football, with a focus on its contribution to evaluating team performance, tactical behavior, and player interactions. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search was conducted across four databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus) from January 2017 to October 2024. Results: Fifty-five peer-reviewed studies met the inclusion criteria, addressing network analysis in official men's professional football matches. Data were extracted and summarized regarding methodological quality, network metrics used, tactical context, and practical implications. Discussion: Most studies demonstrated that cohesive network structures, characterized by high density, clustering coefficients, and centrality, are associated with successful team performance. Centrality metrics were frequently used to identify key tactical players, typically central defenders and midfielders. Recent methodological advances included dynamic time-window analysis, pitch-passing networks, and spatial-temporal integration using tracking data. However, there remains an overrepresentation of elite men's football and offensive phases, with limited focus on defensive networks, youth categories, and women's football. SNA offers a powerful framework to decode the complexity of football performance, evolving from static graphs to dynamic, rolesensitive, and context-rich models. Future research should adopt longitudinal designs, multi-layer network approaches, and closer collaboration with practitioners to enhance the operational utility of network insights in coaching and performance analysis. Systematic review registration: https://osf.io/2pe3y.
objective: Sintetizar cómo se ha usado el análisis de redes sociales (SNA) en fútbol para evaluar rendimiento colectivo, comportamiento táctico e interacciones entre jugadores.
design: Revisión sistemática PRISMA (preregistrada en OSF), búsqueda en PubMed, Scopus, WoS y SPORTDiscus de enero 2017 a octubre 2024.
population: 55 estudios incluidos (de 2.327 registros) sobre partidos oficiales de fútbol profesional masculino; Portugal aporta el 30,9 % de los trabajos.
method: Dos revisores extrajeron métricas de red, contexto táctico e implicaciones prácticas y valoraron la calidad metodológica con una lista de criterios propia (media 73,9 %).
results: El 65 % de los estudios (n=36) fue de calidad excelente y ninguno bajó del 50 %. Las redes cohesionadas (más densidad, agrupamiento y centralidad) se asocian al éxito; la centralidad suele señalar a centrales y centrocampistas. Aparecen avances como ventanas temporales dinámicas, redes por zonas del campo y tracking.
conclusions: El SNA pasa de grafos estáticos a modelos dinámicos y sensibles al rol, pero se necesitan diseños longitudinales, redes multicapa y trabajo conjunto con profesionales.
limitations: Predomina el fútbol masculino de élite y la fase ofensiva; casi no hay defensa, categorías de formación ni fútbol femenino.
why: Es un mapa actual de cómo se mide la coordinación colectiva como sistema complejo en fútbol, útil como base para tus propias lecturas de redes de pase.
practice: Puedes usar densidad y centralidad como indicadores para comparar cómo tus juegos reducidos cambian las conexiones entre jugadores; reconoce el vacío en categorías de formación.
summary: Revisión de 55 estudios que muestra que las redes de pase más densas y cohesionadas se asocian al rendimiento, y que el campo avanza hacia modelos dinámicos con tracking. Faltan estudios en defensa, base y fútbol femenino.

title: From rigid marks to robust perception: Practice variability fosters flexible time-to-contact timing in a virtual reality relay simulator
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: The 4×100-meter relay presents a fundamental motor paradox: maximizing running speed while ensuring millisecond-precision baton transmission. Traditionally, receivers start when their partner reaches a fixed ground mark, a time-to-passage (TTP) strategy that makes them vulnerable to fluctuations in the partner's approach speed. This study evaluated an immersive virtual reality (VR) relay simulator in which receivers learned to initiate their run at a critical time-to-contact (TTC) with the incoming partner, without any ground mark. Twenty-two novice participants practiced with self-controlled feedback, either at a constant approach speed (stable group) or at three approach speeds varying from trial to trial (variable group). All completed a pre-test, acquisition, a post-test, a five-day retention test and a transfer test at a novel approach speed. Absolute timing error decreased significantly between pre-test and retention in both groups, validating task learning. At transfer, however, accuracy declined markedly in the stable group, whereas the variable group maintained its previously acquired accuracy. The constant error of the stable group (+162 ms) closely matched the value predicted if run initiation relied on an optical correlate of distance (+160 ms), while the near-zero constant error of the variable group (+13 ms) indicated reliance on information about TTC. Practice variability thus breaks the confound between TTC and lower-order optical variables, promoting the use of more robust optical information and behavioral flexibility. Shifting from TTP to TTC-based training in VR offers a promising alternative to rigid ground marks for relay training.
