objective: Evaluar desde fuera el modelo de juego «Players First» de la federación austriaca: si sus roles distinguen equipos y si las tareas recomendadas son coherentes.
design: Estudio observacional con datos de posición y eventos.
population: 402 partidos de la Eurocopa masculina 2024, Eurocopa femenina 2025, Liga de Naciones 2025 y clasificación del Mundial 2026.
method: Asignación de jugadores a 4 roles con balón y 4 sin balón según su posición respecto al balón y al área; PERMANOVA por equipo y formación; análisis geométrico y métricas de Espacio Accesible Peligroso (DAS).
results: La identidad del equipo explica varianza significativa en la distribución de roles ofensivos (R² = 0,29, p < 0,001); el resto de resultados no lo he podido leer (el resumen disponible está cortado).
conclusions: No disponible
limitations: No disponible
why: Contrasta con datos de tracking un modelo de juego basado en roles y espacio, útil si analizas cómo se organiza colectivamente un equipo.
practice: Sirve de idea para auditar con vídeo o tracking si los roles que pides en tu modelo de juego aparecen realmente en el partido.
summary: Comunicación que pone a prueba con 402 partidos el modelo «Players First» de la federación austriaca; los roles distinguen a los equipos (R² = 0,29). Solo he leído el resumen parcial.

title: Reference values for collective tactical behaviours based on positional data in professional football matches: a systematic review
abstract: Match collective tactical behaviours can be used as a reference to design and select training strategies to improve individual and team performance in professional football.The aim of the systematic review was to cluster the collective tactical variables used to highlight and compare male soccer teams' collective behaviour during professional official matches, providing reference values for each of them.A systematic review of relevant articles was carried out using three electronic databases (PubMed, SPORTdiscus and Web of Science).From a total of 1,187 studies initially found, 13 original articles were included in the qualitative synthesis.The articles found concerned studies carried out on the Spanish, Portuguese, English and Brazilian 1 st divisions and during the European UEFA Champions League.The team length and width ranged from 31 to 46 m and from 35 to 48 m, respectively.The distance from a defending team's goalkeeper to the nearest teammate ranged from 9 ± 6 to 30 ± 7 m, the goal line-recovery location from 27 to 37 m, and the opponent's goal line from 42 to 50 m.The stretch index ranged from 7 to 16 m.Mean team area was ~900 m 2 and the area of the pitch which included all outfield players divided by the 20 outfield players ranged from 79 ± 15 to 94 ± 16 m 2 .All studies provided greater distance and area values during the team-possession phase in comparison to the non-possession one.The ball location on the pitch determined the collective tactical behaviour of the teams.The differences between halves in the distance and area values were contradictory.Further studies should assess the effect of the interaction between the contextual factors on the collective tactical behaviour to obtain more accurate references.This could help football coaches in the design of
objective: Agrupar las variables tácticas colectivas usadas para comparar equipos de fútbol masculino profesional en partidos oficiales y ofrecer valores de referencia.
design: Revisión sistemática (PubMed, SPORTDiscus, Web of Science).
population: 13 artículos de 1.187 hallados; primeras divisiones de España, Portugal, Inglaterra y Brasil y Champions League.
method: Clasificación de variables colectivas basadas en posición (longitud, anchura, área, estiramiento, distancias a portería) y recopilación de sus valores por fase de juego.
results: Longitud 31–46 m y anchura 35–48 m; área media del equipo ~900 m²; índice de estiramiento 7–16 m. Todas las medidas son mayores con posesión que sin ella y la posición del balón condiciona el comportamiento colectivo; las diferencias entre partes son contradictorias.
conclusions: Estos valores sirven de referencia para diseñar tareas de entrenamiento; faltan estudios sobre la interacción de factores contextuales.
limitations: Solo 13 estudios, heterogéneos en métricas y contextos.
why: Tienes cifras concretas de comportamiento colectivo (amplitud, profundidad, área) para ajustar las dimensiones de tus juegos y compararlas con el partido real; sigue vigente como base de los estudios posicionales actuales.
practice: Dimensiona campos de juego reducido usando áreas por jugador cercanas a las de competición (~80–95 m² por jugador de campo).
summary: Revisión sistemática de 13 estudios que reúne valores de referencia de comportamiento táctico colectivo en fútbol profesional (longitud, anchura, área, estiramiento) y su variación con la posesión.

title: Designing small-sided games for counter-attack training in youth soccer
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: The present study aimed to test different designs of counter-attacking training on tactical behaviour by manipulating the number of players and time pressure (limitation on the duration of the players’ offensive action). Specifically, we compared the influence of time pressure and numerical superiority (through an additional player) on the players’ performance and tactical behaviour in small-sided games (SSGs). Forty under-17 soccer athletes participated in the study. The athletes performed 4 SSGs in the following configurations: numerical equality and time pressure (GR-4 × 4-GR – TP); numerical equality and no time pressure (GR-4 × 4-GR – NTP); numerical superiority and time pressure (GR-5 × 4-GR – TP) and numerical superiority and no time pressure (GR-5 × 4-GR – NTP). Tactical performance was evaluated using the Game Performance Evaluation Tool (GPET), and tactical behaviour using positional data measured by the Global Positioning System. The statistical analysis was performed using two-way repeated measures analysis of variance. There was a better tactical performance in decision-making (0.669 ± 0.135, p = .02 and r = .27) and execution (0.602 ± 0.134, p = .002 and r = .44) of technical-tactical actions in the SSG without the time pressure rule. Furthermore, the space exploration index showed lower values (5.634 ± 0.604, p = .007 and r = .32) in games with time pressure than in games without this rule, and there were no significant differences for player length and width behaviour between protocols. It is concluded that the time pressure rule reduces the exploratory behaviour of the players. Understanding these effects allows coaches to plan better training sessions that address the contents of counter-attacks in SSG.
objective: Probar cómo la presión de tiempo y la superioridad numérica modifican el rendimiento y el comportamiento táctico en juegos reducidos de contraataque.
design: Experimental intra-sujeto, 4 configuraciones de juego reducido.
population: 40 futbolistas sub-17.
method: 4 formatos (4v4 y 5v4, con y sin presión de tiempo); rendimiento táctico con GPET y comportamiento con posiciones GPS; ANOVA de medidas repetidas de dos factores.
results: Sin presión de tiempo mejoraron la toma de decisiones (0,669 ± 0,135; p = 0,02; r = 0,27) y la ejecución (0,602 ± 0,134; p = 0,002; r = 0,44), y el índice de exploración del espacio fue mayor (5,634 ± 0,604 con presión; p = 0,007); no hubo diferencias en longitud y anchura.
conclusions: La regla de presión de tiempo reduce la conducta exploratoria de los jugadores.
limitations: Una sola muestra sub-17 y tareas breves; sin evaluación de transferencia al partido.
why: Es un ejemplo limpio de manipular una restricción (tiempo) y ver cómo cambia la exploración, justo el razonamiento del CLA.
practice: Si quieres decisiones de calidad en transiciones, evita imponer límites de tiempo estrictos; úsalos solo cuando busques velocidad de ejecución.
summary: 40 sub-17 jugaron cuatro juegos reducidos de contraataque. La presión de tiempo empeoró decisión y ejecución y redujo la exploración del espacio; la superioridad numérica no cambió longitud ni anchura.

title: Impacto de la metodología no lineal sobre variables técnicas y cinemáticas en el entrenamiento de fútbol
venue: Journal of Sport and Health Research
objective: Analizar la influencia de una metodología no lineal sobre variables técnicas y cinemáticas del entrenamiento de fútbol.
design: Comparación de dos tareas (tradicional analítica vs no lineal) durante 3 semanas, cada tarea observada 8 veces; 8 minutos por tarea.
population: 22 futbolistas semiprofesionales masculinos, 21,24 ± 1,86 años y 12 años de experiencia, España.
method: Mismo espacio (40×40 m), mismo número de jugadores y mismos elementos técnicos en ambas tareas. Variables: pase, control y tiro (vídeo), tiempo de participación y GPS a 10 Hz (distancia total, tres rangos de velocidad, aceleraciones y deceleraciones > 2 m/s²).
results: La metodología no lineal mostró diferencias significativas a su favor en distancia total (p < 0,001), distancias <14 km/h (p = 0,034), 14–22,3 km/h (p = 0,003) y aceleraciones (p = 0,017), además de más acciones de pase y control y mayor RPE (p = 0,023).
conclusions: Los métodos no lineales podrían generar mayor impacto en el desarrollo de habilidades en el juego que los tradicionales, con más y más funcionales experiencias con balón.
limitations: No se distingue por posición, la tarea es breve (8 min) y las tareas no están igualadas más allá del espacio y los jugadores; los autores reconocen estas limitaciones.
why: Compara directamente una tarea analítica con una no lineal midiendo técnica y carga física con GPS, en castellano y con jugadores adultos.
practice: Sustituye parte del trabajo analítico por un juego en el mismo espacio y con los mismos elementos técnicos: obtendrás más contactos con balón y más carga a velocidad media.
summary: 22 semiprofesionales realizaron tareas tradicionales y no lineales en 40×40 m; la no lineal produjo más acciones técnicas y más distancia y aceleraciones, aunque el diseño es breve y sin control posicional.

title: Context-dependent velocity distributions in professional soccer: Players, referees, and ball conduction
abstract: Quantifying locomotor demands in soccer is essential for understanding performance, fatigue, and the physical demands experienced by players and referees throughout the competition. While prior research has typically focused on isolated intensity metrics such as sprint distance or high-speed running, less attention has been given to the full distribution of movement velocities and how these distributions vary across playing roles, match contexts, and interactions with the ball. Here, we analyse optical tracking data from 100 professional LaLiga matches (2019/2020 season), including 362 outfield players and goalkeepers, 100 main referee performances, and 200 assistant referee performances. Instantaneous velocities were derived from positional data sampled at 25 Hz, and probability distribution functions were used to characterise locomotor regimes across match halves, attacking and defending phases, and ball-conduction situations. The results show a consistent reduction in player speed during the second half, which is explained mainly by an increased probability of walking and a decreased probability of jogging. The main referees display a comparable tendency, whereas the assistant referees show the opposite pattern, increasing the jogging frequency during the second half. Tactical context also modulates movement patterns: During attacking phases, most players increase the probability of walking, whereas goalkeepers increase their locomotor intensity. When conducting the ball, players across all positions move faster than they do during attacking phases without possession, reducing walking and increasing jogging. Overall, this study provides a detailed description of movement–velocity distributions in elite soccer and highlights the interplay between physical load, tactic
summary: Distribuciones de velocidad con tracking óptico de 100 partidos de LaLiga para jugadores y árbitros; enfoque de carga física.
why: Tangencial: carga física sin componente de aprendizaje.

title: The Future of Skill Acquisition
abstract: The Constraints-Led Approach (CLA) posits that behaviour emerges during learning and development through various interacting constraints, allowing individuals to exploit inherent tendencies for self-organisation. This framework has garnered significant attention from academics and practitioners interested in skill acquisition. Over the past 40 years, the continued development of theory and practice associated with CLA has enhanced its engagement and application within the sport sciences. As a result, numerous national sports organisations, professional teams, and individual coaches have adopted CLA principles in practice across a diverse range of sports, including professional football, the NBA, American football, canoeing, dance, figure skating, team sports, swimming, and golf. However, this alternative approach has led to several questions for advocates and practitioners wishing to implement CLA principles. In this chapter, we explore these challenges, framing them as opportunities for practitioners interested in adopting and applying CLA principles in their own work. By embracing these challenges, practitioners can deepen their understanding of skill acquisition and enhance their effectiveness in coaching and athlete development.
objective: Analizar los retos que plantea aplicar el Constraints-Led Approach (CLA) en la práctica y plantearlos como oportunidades.
design: Capítulo teórico-aplicado de libro (Routledge).
population: No aplica
method: Revisión narrativa de cómo se ha adoptado el CLA en federaciones, equipos profesionales y entrenadores de distintos deportes (fútbol profesional, NBA, natación, golf, danza…).
results: Los autores identifican preguntas recurrentes de quienes quieren implementar el CLA y las reformulan como oportunidades para profundizar en la comprensión de la adquisición de habilidades. No se aportan cifras en el abstract.
conclusions: Asumir esos retos ayuda a los practicantes a entender mejor el CLA y a mejorar su aplicación.
limitations: Solo he podido leer el abstract; capítulo de acceso restringido y sin datos empíricos propios.
why: Está firmado por Renshaw, Rothwell y Davids: es la visión de los autores de referencia sobre hacia dónde va el CLA, justo tu línea central.
practice: Úsalo como guía de preguntas frecuentes antes de rediseñar tareas con restricciones en tu equipo.
summary: Capítulo de cierre del libro que repasa 40 años de CLA y convierte las dificultades de implementarlo en oportunidades de práctica. Recoge su adopción en deportes y clubes de élite.

title: A History of Skill Acquisition
abstract: This chapter discusses major historical influences on the field of skill acquisition that have shaped theory and practice. An initial stimulus on skill acquisition theory was pre-scientific introspection, reflection, and debate on human identity, existence, and experience by early philosophers, intellectuals, and artists. Understanding where skill acquisition theories have emerged from, especially their distinct philosophical and meta-theoretical foundations, is essential for comparing their value for practical applications in education, therapy, training, and coaching. In skill acquisition, different theories have distinct metatheoretical roots (with distinct philosophical and scientific origins and assumptions). Applying theoretical principles in practice implies acceptance of the metatheoretical assumptions underlying a particular theory. Since metatheories have distinct assumptions and beliefs, it could be illogical and incoherent to integrate concepts, ideas, methods, and principles from different theories to apply in practice. Practitioners working in skill acquisition need to be aware of the invisible golden threads of meta-theoretical logic that need to be respected and cannot be entangled (through inter-mixing key ideas from different theories) because that could lead to incoherence in how practitioners conceptualise learners and the learning process. Arguments against uncritical integration raise serious concerns about the risks of blending ideas, concepts, and tools from distinct theories without careful consideration. These risks include using contradictory and less effective practices in the professional work of coaches, trainers, and skill acquisition specialists when intentionally selecting concepts and methods advocated in different scientific theories.
objective: Repasar las influencias históricas y metateóricas que han moldeado las teorías de adquisición de habilidades.
design: Capítulo teórico de libro (Routledge).
population: No aplica
method: Recorrido histórico desde la reflexión filosófica pre-científica hasta las teorías actuales, comparando sus supuestos metateóricos.
results: Argumentan que cada teoría descansa en supuestos metateóricos distintos, por lo que mezclar conceptos de teorías diferentes en la práctica puede ser incoherente.
conclusions: Quien aplique una teoría debe aceptar y respetar sus supuestos de base.
limitations: Solo abstract leído; enfoque teórico y posicionado (Davids y colegas).
why: Te da el marco para justificar por qué CLA/dinámica ecológica no es compatible con mezclar métodos de teorías cognitivas o conductistas sin criterio.
summary: Historia de las teorías de adquisición de habilidades y sus raíces filosóficas. Defiende la coherencia metateórica al llevarlas a la práctica.

title: Skill Acquisition in Team Sport
abstract: This chapter explains how team sport players require the ability to outwit their opponent, which is a key element of game understanding. In doing so, players require different knowledge and skills, which at the highest level involves players being strategic about what action to take next and why. Drawing from principles of video game design, the chapter introduces two different sport coaching methods: Digital Video Game Design (DVGD) and Gamification. This chapter explains how these methods have different purposes, presenting them both as viable tools for coaches to consider in team sport coaching contexts. DVGD emphasises player problem-solving skills using pedagogical principles such as superpowers, level-ups, and pauses, while Gamification promotes engaging in skill execution with challenges and rewards. Findings from applying DVGD and Gamification from a case study example in youth soccer demonstrated how individual players within the team experienced different challenges and benefits when engaging with the two named coaching methods. In summary, this chapter provides real-world insight into how team sport coaches can think critically about how to use principles of video game design in their coaching practice to enhance how players outwit their opponent, whilst appreciating there is no ‘one size fits all’ coaching method.
objective: Presentar dos métodos de coaching en deportes de equipo basados en el diseño de videojuegos: Digital Video Game Design (DVGD) y gamificación.
design: Capítulo de libro con estudio de caso en fútbol juvenil.
population: Jugadores de un equipo de fútbol juvenil (n no indicado en el abstract).
method: Aplicación de DVGD (superpoderes, subidas de nivel, pausas) y de gamificación (retos y recompensas) en un caso de fútbol juvenil.
results: Cada jugador vivió retos y beneficios distintos con cada método: DVGD enfatiza la resolución de problemas y la gamificación la ejecución con retos.
conclusions: Ambos son herramientas viables que el entrenador debe elegir de forma crítica según su propósito.
limitations: Estudio de caso; solo abstract leído, sin datos cuantitativos.
why: Conecta pedagogía centrada en problemas con tu campo de fútbol juvenil.
practice: Prueba a estructurar una sesión con niveles de dificultad y 'pausas' para que los jugadores resuelvan el problema táctico.
summary: Dos métodos inspirados en videojuegos para entrenar deportes de equipo, probados en fútbol juvenil con resultados diferentes por jugador.

title: Skill Acquisition in Practice
abstract: The role of Skill Acquisition Specialists (SAS) within high-performance sport has evolved significantly since their emergence in the early 2000s. While recent literature has attempted to define the SAS role, less attention has been paid to how their professional practice influences coach development, practice design, and athlete performance. This chapter explores SAS practice through three practitioner perspectives, highlighting decision-making as a critical pillar of effective support. Each perspective illustrates distinct approaches (e.g., professional judgment and decision-making, espoused theory/theory-in-use for guiding coach learning, and design thinking for collaborative practice design) while emphasising a coach focus that is flexible and contextually relevant. We suggest that SAS effectiveness depends not only on technical expertise but also on relational, communication, and adaptive skills that enable specialists to navigate complex, uncertain environments. A comparative analysis of these approaches reveals a spectrum of engagement styles shaped by perceived roles and aims. The chapter concludes by identifying future priorities, including refining SAS competencies, enhancing decision-making development, and optimising organisational integration. By shifting the focus from defining the role to understanding how SASs work in practice, this work contributes to exploring the impact of skill acquisition within sporting systems.
objective: Explorar la práctica de los especialistas en adquisición de habilidades (SAS) en deporte de alto rendimiento y su influencia en el desarrollo de entrenadores y el diseño de práctica.
design: Capítulo con tres perspectivas de practicantes.
population: No aplica (tres practicantes SAS).
method: Comparación de enfoques: juicio profesional y toma de decisiones, teoría espoused/in-use y design thinking.
results: La eficacia del SAS depende de habilidades relacionales, comunicativas y adaptativas, además de la técnica.
conclusions: Se proponen prioridades futuras para refinar competencias del SAS.
limitations: Solo abstract; perspectivas personales, no datos empíricos.
why: Si trabajas con entrenadores en el diseño de práctica, describe cómo hacerlo de forma colaborativa.
practice: Aplica el co-diseño de tareas con tu cuerpo técnico.
summary: Tres miradas de especialistas en adquisición de habilidades sobre cómo apoyar a entrenadores y diseñar práctica.

title: Skill Acquisition in Learning
abstract: Skilled motor performance is often described as the product of automatic processes that operate outside conscious awareness. This perspective has been particularly influential in sport psychology, where conscious control is frequently associated with performance disruption, choking under pressure, and reinvestment in movement mechanics. However, emerging theoretical and empirical work suggests that this view may be overly simplistic. Conscious processes do not disappear with expertise; rather, they change in form and function. This chapter critically examines the role of conscious control in skilled movement, drawing on research from motor learning, sport psychology, and cognitive science. We argue that conscious engagement in performance exists along a continuum, ranging from detailed movement monitoring to higher-level strategic, attentional, and reflective processes. While directing attention to specific movement mechanics can disrupt well-learned skills, other forms of conscious engagement, such as situational awareness, rhythm regulation, or tactical decision-making, may support performance and adaptability. We also discuss how individual differences, such as propensity for reinvestment, and contextual factors, such as pressure or novelty, influence when conscious control becomes helpful or harmful. Finally, we outline practical implications for coaching and training, emphasising the importance of developing athletes’ capacity to regulate conscious engagement across different stages of skill development and performance contexts rather than attempting to eliminate conscious control altogether.
objective: Examinar el papel del control consciente en el movimiento experto.
design: Capítulo teórico de libro.
population: No aplica
method: Revisión crítica de motor learning, psicología del deporte y ciencia cognitiva.
results: El control consciente es un continuo: dirigir la atención a la mecánica perturba habilidades aprendidas, pero la conciencia situacional, el ritmo o la decisión táctica pueden ayudar.
conclusions: La visión de que la pericia es solo automática es demasiado simple.
limitations: Solo abstract; teórico.
why: Matiza los debates sobre foco de atención y reinversión que influyen en tus instrucciones al jugador.
practice: Prefiere señales sobre el entorno y la decisión antes que instrucciones sobre la mecánica.
summary: El control consciente no desaparece con la pericia sino que cambia de forma; no todo es perjudicial.

title: Coach-led questioning and tactical decision-making in youth soccer, basketball, and volleyball: proposed cognitive pathways and contextual boundaries
abstract: Coach-led questioning is widely advocated in game-based training for youth soccer, basketball, and volleyball, yet its implications for tactical decision-making and cognitive load remain uncertain. This mini review critically integrates coaching observations, instructional contrasts, and adjacent cognitive studies to examine whether questions provide cognitive scaffolding or competing processing demands under differing expertise, task constraints, and timing. A meta-analysis of game-based approaches (28 studies; 1,600 participants overall) reported an 11.41-percentage-point advantage in decision-making (95% CI 4.39–18.43), based on 17 contributing studies, but did not isolate questioning. Observations of 19 youth soccer coaches recorded 71 questions per session on average, with only 7% of divergent prompts explicitly asking players to solve problems. In a school basketball comparison ( n = 37), post-test appropriate decision scores favored questioning over prescriptive feedback for passing (0.900 vs. 0.823; p = 0.026) and shooting (0.958 vs. 0.801; p = 0.003). Across these studies, instructional components frequently co-varied, limiting attribution to questioning and leaving cognitive-load mediation untested. We propose potentially co-occurring attentional scaffolding and verbal-processing competition, and recommend trials independently manipulating question content and timing while measuring cognitive processing and delayed game transfer.
objective: Valorar si las preguntas del entrenador mejoran la toma de decisiones táctica en jóvenes de fútbol, baloncesto y voleibol.
design: Mini-revisión crítica con propuesta de vías cognitivas.
population: Integra un meta-análisis previo (28 estudios, 1.600 participantes), observación de 19 entrenadores de fútbol juvenil y una comparación escolar en baloncesto (n=37).
method: Integración de observaciones, contrastes instruccionales y estudios cognitivos adyacentes.
results: Los enfoques basados en juegos mejoran la decisión +11,41 puntos porcentuales (IC95% 4,39–18,43) sin aislar el efecto de preguntar. Los entrenadores hacían 71 preguntas por sesión y solo el 7% de las divergentes pedía resolver problemas. En baloncesto, preguntar superó al feedback prescriptivo en pase (0,900 vs 0,823; p=0,026) y tiro (0,958 vs 0,801; p=0,003).
conclusions: Preguntar puede ser andamiaje atencional o competir por recursos de procesamiento; hacen falta ensayos que manipulen contenido y momento de la pregunta.
limitations: Componentes instruccionales co-varían y la carga cognitiva no se midió.
why: Aborda directamente cómo preguntar sin prescribir en pedagogía no lineal.
practice: Reduce preguntas rutinarias, formula pocas y abiertas, y cuida el momento para no interrumpir el juego.
summary: Revisión crítica sobre si las preguntas del entrenador ayudan a decidir mejor. La evidencia es prometedora pero no aísla el efecto.

title: Correspondence Between Small-Sided Games Implementation and Competitive Ball Progression in Elite Football: A Retrospective Case Study
authors: I Dewa Made Arya Nanda Wijaya Kusuma
abstract: Background & objective: Small-sided games (SSGs) are widely used in football because they manipulate player numbers, playing area, rules, while preserving key features of match play. However, evidence linking SSG implementation to ball progression during elite competition remains limited when SSGs are embedded in a real-world preparation programme rather than imposed experimentally. This study examined the correspondence between SSG implementation and ball progression performance in the East Java Provincial Football Team during the 2024 National Sports Week (PON XXI). Materials & Methods: A quantitative ex post facto performance-analysis design was used. Official training documentation, match recordings, match statistics, were reviewed. The performance dataset comprised three PON matches against Papua Pegunungan, West Java, and Aceh. SSG implementation was characterised by player-number modification, playing-area manipulation, game constraints, intensity, and training objectives. Ball progression was assessed using passing accuracy, attacking-third passes, successful progressive passes, through passes, and chances created. Descriptive statistics were used because the available dataset did not support a valid participant-level inferential model. STROBE was used as the reporting framework. Results: Across the three analysed matches, possession ranged from 31% to 47% and passing accuracy from 63.46% to 72.87%. Successful progressive passes ranged from 19 to 40, successful attacking-third passes from 80 to 115, and chances created from 2 to 7. Progressive passing and through passes were present in all three matches. objective: Examinar la correspondencia entre juegos reducidos y la progresión de balón en fútbol de élite.
design: Estudio de caso retrospectivo (ex post facto), análisis de rendimiento, STROBE.
population: Selección provincial de Java Oriental, 3 partidos de PON XXI 2024 (Indonesia).
method: Documentación de entrenamiento y estadísticas de partido; SSG caracterizados por número de jugadores, área, restricciones e intensidad; progresión medida con pases precisos, al tercio final, progresivos, filtrados y ocasiones. Estadística descriptiva.

why: Relaciona manipulación de restricciones en SSG con rendimiento en competición.

summary: Caso de una selección provincial que muestra coherencia entre sus juegos reducidos y la progresión de balón, sin causalidad probada.

title: PENGEMBANGAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN SEPAK BOLA BERBASIS TGfU MELALUI SMALL-SIDED GAMES UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN TEKNIK DAN TACTICAL AWARENESS MAHASISWA PENDIDIKAN JASMANI
abstract: Football courses in physical education study programs are still dominated by isolated technical drills, so that students master techniques in closed situations but struggle to apply them during game play. This study aimed to develop a football learning model based on Teaching Games for Understanding (TGfU) through small-sided games and to test its effectiveness in improving technical skills and tactical awareness. A research and development design adapted from Borg and Gall was carried out in three stages: preliminary study, model development and validation, and effectiveness testing. The model consists of six syntactical steps, namely game, game appreciation, tactical awareness, decision making, skill execution, and performance. The model was validated by three experts and tried out on 12 students. Effectiveness was tested using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design involving 56 students (28 experimental and 28 control). Data were analyzed using N-Gain, independent samples t-test, Cohen’s d, and MANOVA. The model was rated highly feasible (88.8%), with 91.7% syntax implementation and 87.4% practicality. The experimental group achieved a higher N-Gain than the control group in technical skills (0.51 vs 0.25; t = 6.47; p < 0.001; d = 1.73) and tactical awareness (0.50 vs 0.20; t = 7.98; p < 0.001; d = 2.13), with a significant simultaneous effect (Wilks’ Lambda = 0.512; F(2,53) = 25.27; p < 0.001). The model is feasible, practical, and effective, and equips prospective physical education teachers with a game-based framework that can be adapted for football lessons in elementary schools.
objective: Desarrollar y probar un modelo de enseñanza de fútbol basado en TGfU mediante juegos reducidos.
design: I+D (Borg y Gall) y cuasi-experimento pretest-postest con grupo control.
population: 56 estudiantes de educación física (28/28); validación con 3 expertos y prueba piloto con 12 (Indonesia).
method: Modelo de seis pasos: juego, apreciación, conciencia táctica, decisión, ejecución y rendimiento; N-Gain, t, d de Cohen y MANOVA.
results: Viabilidad 88,8%. N-Gain técnico 0,51 vs 0,25 (d=1,73) y táctico 0,50 vs 0,20 (d=2,13); efecto conjunto Wilks' Lambda=0,512 (p<0,001).
conclusions: El modelo es viable, práctico y eficaz.
limitations: Muestra pequeña de estudiantes universitarios, sin seguimiento a largo plazo.
why: Ejemplo de enseñanza game-based que parte del juego, afín a la pedagogía no lineal.
practice: Adapta la secuencia juego → decisión → ejecución en tus sesiones.
summary: Un modelo TGfU con juegos reducidos mejora técnica y conciencia táctica frente a la enseñanza habitual.

title: Goalkeeper coaches' decision-making in back-pass situations: comparing 2D, video, and immersive virtual reality perspectives
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Coaching, Sport Psychology, Motor Control, Learning, and Behavior Keywords: decision making, Football, virtual reality, perceptual cognitive, Visual exploratory activity, goalkeeper In modern football, goalkeepers play an increasingly central role in build-up play, requiring advanced perceptual–cognitive skills to manage back-pass situations. While decision-making and visual exploratory activity (VEA) have been widely studied in outfield players, goalkeeper-specific evidence remains limited, particularly in immersive virtual reality (VR) environments. This study examined whether immersive VR preserves the consistency of expert goalkeeper coaches' decision-making compared with traditional visualization modalities (2D overhead and broadcast video), and whether VEA in VR predicts decision consistency. Thirty-three expert goalkeeper coaches evaluated back-pass situations across three visualization conditions (2D, video, VR) and two game plans (Maintain Possession, Advance Play). Decision selection, inter- and intra-rater agreement were recorded. Inter-rater agreement was comparable across visualization modalities for both Maintain Possession (α=0.54 to 0.60) and Advance Play decisions (α=0.39 to 0.42), with no significant between-condition differences. Importantly, higher VEA in VR predicted greater alignment with peer expert consensus for Advance Play decisions and higher VEA was significantly but weakly correlated with intra-rater decision consistency for both Maintain Possession and Advance Play decisions. These findings suggest that immersive VR preserves expert decision structures while promoting active information-seeking behaviors that become decision-critical under high tactical complexity.
objective: Comprobar si la realidad virtual inmersiva mantiene la consistencia de decisión de entrenadores de porteros frente a 2D y vídeo.
design: Preprint, estudio transversal intra-sujeto.
population: 33 entrenadores de porteros expertos.
method: Evaluación de situaciones de cesión al portero en 2D, vídeo y RV con dos planes de juego; acuerdo inter e intra-evaluador y actividad exploratoria visual (VEA).
results: Acuerdo similar entre modalidades (α=0,54–0,60 mantener posesión; 0,39–0,42 avanzar). Mayor VEA en RV predijo mayor alineación con el consenso experto en 'avanzar'.
conclusions: La RV preserva las estructuras de decisión expertas y fomenta la búsqueda de información.
limitations: Acuerdo moderado-bajo; preprint sin revisión por pares.
why: Conecta percepción-acción y decisión del portero en construcción.
practice: Usa RV o vídeo para entrenar la exploración visual de porteros.
summary: La RV mantiene la consistencia de decisión de expertos y favorece la exploración visual en cesiones.

title: A Narrative Review of Sport Specific Focus of Attention Instructions on Athlete Sport Skill Performance.
abstract: The purpose of the present narrative review was to synthesize the available findings from research examining sport specific focus of attention instructions on the performance of Tier 3 and Tier 4 athletes on sport specific motor tasks. Thirteen empirical studies were identified as meeting the eligibility criteria for this narrative review. Our review of the research showed mixed support for an advantage of an external focus of attention for the performance of sport specific skills, independent of the classification of the motor task (i.e. discrete or continuous). The remaining research reviewed showed motor performance was similar for the athletes when provided external or internal focus of attention instructions. These findings, together with recent concerns regarding reporting bias in the broader focus-of-attention literature, suggest that claims regarding the consistent superiority of an external focus should be interpreted cautiously. The findings from our review highlighted the impact of task relevant content in modulating the effectiveness of the instructional statements, and the importance of providing the athlete control over the focus of attention instructions. There was limited theoretical interpretation of findings when motor performance was similar for internal and external focus of attention instructions. Evidence-based practical implications are suggested for the coach and athlete.
objective: Sintetizar el efecto de las instrucciones de foco atencional en habilidades específicas de atletas de nivel alto.
design: Revisión narrativa.
population: 13 estudios empíricos con atletas Tier 3 y 4.
method: Síntesis de estudios sobre foco externo vs interno en tareas discretas y continuas.
results: Apoyo mixto a la ventaja del foco externo; en el resto el rendimiento fue similar. Importa el contenido de la instrucción y el control del atleta.
conclusions: Hay que interpretar con cautela la superioridad del foco externo, dado el posible sesgo de publicación.
limitations: Pocos estudios; abstract leído, texto de pago.
why: Matiza la dogmática del foco externo que se usa en coaching.
practice: Ofrece al jugador elegir el tipo de instrucción y adapta la señal a la tarea.
summary: La ventaja del foco externo en atletas de nivel alto es menos consistente de lo que se suele afirmar.

title: Associations between accumulated weekly external load and technical match actions in elite soccer
abstract: This study investigated the associations between accumulated weekly external load metrics and match technical performance in elite male players.19 outfield players from a Brazilian first-division club (25.7 ± 3.9 years; 80.4 ± 6.6 kg; 181.3 ± 6.7 cm) were monitored across 208 sessions (170 training sessions and 38 official matches) during a full competitive season.External load was quantified, capturing total distance (TD), PlayerLoad (PL), high-speed running distance (HSRD), total accelerations (ACC), and repeated high-intensity efforts (RHIE).Match technical performance was categorized into defensive and offensive indicators.Results showed several negative associations between accumulated weekly external load and technical performance indicators.TD was negatively associated with Clearances (β = -0.310)and Successful Forward Passes (β = -0.213),while PL was negatively associated with Clearances (β = -0.315)and Aerial Duels Won (β = -0.216).Additionally, HSRD and RHIE were negatively associated with Interceptions (β = -0.273;β = -0.284).Finally, ACC was negatively associated with Interceptions (β = -0.241),Offensive Volume (β = -0.220),and Successful Total Passes (β = -0.207).These results suggest that weeks characterized by higher training volumes and intensities may negatively affect offensive and defensive technical performance in subsequent matches.Consequently, coaches should consider the adequacy of the weekly load composition, specifically managing neuromuscular stress and exposure to high intensity before matches, to balance offensive readiness with technical precision and defensive efficiency.An integrated approach combining external load and technical-tactical monitoring can optimize training prescription and help maintain performance throughout the competitiv
objective: Relacionar la carga externa semanal acumulada con acciones técnicas en partido.
design: Observacional longitudinal, una temporada.
population: 19 jugadores de campo de un club brasileño de primera (25,7±3,9 años), 208 sesiones.
method: Carga externa por GPS (distancia, PlayerLoad, alta velocidad, aceleraciones) frente a indicadores técnicos defensivos y ofensivos.
results: Asociaciones negativas, p. ej. distancia total con despejes (β=-0,310) y aceleraciones con pases totales (β=-0,207).
conclusions: Semanas con más volumen e intensidad pueden empeorar el rendimiento técnico posterior.
limitations: Un solo club y diseño correlacional.
why: Útil para el lado de campo: carga y calidad técnica.
practice: Vigila la carga de alta intensidad antes de partidos.
summary: Mayor carga semanal se asocia a peor rendimiento técnico en partido en un club de élite.

title: Experience and Implications of Japan’s Youth Football Talent Development from the Perspective of Sport–Education Integration
venue: Academic journal of management and social sciences
abstract: In April 2009, the General Administration of Sport of China, together with the Ministry of Education, issued the Notice on Launching the National Youth Campus Football Program and established the National Youth Campus Football Leading Group, thereby initiating a period of rapid development for campus football in China[1]. The General Administration of Sport’s proposed 15th Five-Year Plan regards consolidating the “three major ball sports” as a foundation for development, includes them among the revitalization objectives, and calls for continued football governance reform. Youth football should receive high priority: campus football should continue to expand; the number and quality of coaches should improve at the same time; the five-level youth training centers should develop substantially; the system of competitions should be designed around young people; a Chinese Youth Football League should be established; professional football clubs should operate in a sound manner; and professional leagues should develop healthily[2]. Japan and China are geographically close and have broadly similar population physical fitness, yet their overall football development still shows a clear gap. Japan’s rapid progress and successful rise in football are reflected not only in its higher FIFA ranking but are also closely related to its highly developed youth development system and professional leagues. Its football development did not rely on short-term campaigns; rather, it was achieved gradually through a longer-term approach and a complete system. Starting with youth development, supported by professional leagues, and using organizational development as the means, Japan ensures a continuous emergence of talent. title: Exploring the degeneracy and creativity of passing behaviors from discrete passing variables in small-sided soccer games
abstract: The aim of this study was to explore the degeneracy and creativity of passing behaviors hidden behind the number of passes in small-sided games to inform football coaches’ training programmes. Based on ecological dynamics, the constraint of pitch size was manipulated to incorporate passing numbers, penetrative passing behaviours and creative passing behaviours together in small-sided games. Twenty U-19 male football players played 10 small-sided games on two different sizes of pitches. The results found that the number of passes (p = . 433, Cohen’s d = 0.39, small effect size) and passing fluency (p = .645, Cohen’s d = 0.22, small effect size) did not differ significantly between the two different sizes of pitches; whereas in Pitch 1 (35 m × 20 m), there was more penetrative passing behaviours (p = . 052, Cohen’s d = 1.22, large effect); in Pitch 2 (25 m × 15 m), players emerged with greater versatility in passing behaviours (p = .028, Cohen’s d = 1.50, large effect) and passing attempts (p = .170, Cohen’s d = 0.75, medium effect); and there were two more original passing actions emerging from Pitch 2 than from Pitch 1. This suggest that coaches cannot rely solely on the number of passes to develop players’ passing behaviour in small-sided games.Coaches should deeply understand the eco-dynamic value of passing behaviours, and be skilled at exploring the degeneracy,variability and creativity of passing behaviours in order to develop more scientific training plans and enhance the creativity of soccer players.
objective: Explorar si el tamaño del campo cambia la degeneración y la creatividad de los pases en juegos reducidos, más allá del número de pases.
design: Estudio intra-sujeto (transversal) con dos tamaños de campo, 8 min por partido, durante dos semanas; marco de dinámica ecológica.
population: 20 futbolistas varones sub-19 de un club profesional (17,4 ± 1,3 años; 9,1 ± 0,7 años de práctica); autores de instituciones chinas.
method: Juegos 4 vs 4 sin porteros ni fuera de juego en campo de 35×20 m y de 25×15 m (5 partidos analizados por campo), grabados con dron y codificados; se registraron pases totales, penetrantes y cuatro indicadores de creatividad (fluidez, versatilidad, originalidad, intentos). t de Student pareada y d de Cohen; fiabilidad del codificado ICC 0,88–0,91.
results: El número total de pases no difirió (514 vs 585; p=0,433). En el campo grande hubo más pases penetrantes (79 vs 64; p=0,052; d=1,22) y en el pequeño más versatilidad (11,2 vs 8,2; p=0,028; d=1,50), con 3 tipos de pase originales frente a 1. Originalidad e intentos no alcanzaron significación.
conclusions: Contar pases no basta para valorar el comportamiento de pase; el campo pequeño favorece pases más variables y creativos y el grande los más penetrantes.
limitations: Muestra pequeña y t pareadas sobre datos agregados sin modelar el agrupamiento; varios efectos descansan en p≈0,05 y el texto los presenta como significativos.
why: Es un ejemplo directo de manipular una restricción de tarea (el tamaño del campo) y leer la degeneración y la variabilidad funcional, no solo el volumen de acciones.
practice: Alterna campos de tamaño distinto según quieras pases verticales (más grande) o repertorio variado de pases (más pequeño), y evalúa la variedad de soluciones además del número de pases.
summary: Con 20 sub-19, comparar dos tamaños de campo en 4 vs 4 mostró que el total de pases no cambia, pero sí su naturaleza: más penetración en el grande y más versatilidad y originalidad en el pequeño. Efectos prometedores aunque con muestra pequeña y estadística frágil.

title: ‘An arm around the shoulder or a kick up the backside?’: Athlete perspectives on the expertise coaches require for the coach–athlete relationship in performance football
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: The coach–athlete (C-A) relationship has been explored across multiple disciplines, with coaches’ ability to navigate these relationships widely regarded as central to coaching effectiveness. However, support for developing the expertise required by coaches to build effective C-A relationships remains underrepresented within formal coach education programmes. Increasingly, the C-A relationship is recognised as being shaped by broader socio-cultural contexts, highlighting the need to examine relational processes within the specific environments in which they occur. Significantly, this study foregrounds athletes’ perspectives from the highest levels of the professional game to explore how coaches’ relational expertise is perceived, interpreted, and experienced within C-A relationships. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight male and female professional athletes (n = 4 male, n = 4 female) competing in, or with significant experience of, high-performance football environments. Inductive reflexive thematic analysis generated four themes: (1) Beyond ‘building relationships’: towards a more considered position (2) The self as the cornerstone of relational practice; (3) Challenging dyadic conceptions of the C-A relationship; and (4) Developing relational astuteness: noticing, negotiating and influencing. The paper provides important contextually situated, athlete-centred insights into the expertise coaches require to develop effective C-A relationships.

results: Cuatro temas: ir más allá de 'construir relación'; el propio entrenador como base de la práctica relacional; cuestionar la visión diádica de la relación; y desarrollar 'astucia relacional' (percibir, negociar e influir).

summary: Entrevistas a 8 futbolistas profesionales identifican cuatro temas sobre la pericia relacional que necesitan los entrenadores, resaltando el contexto y la lectura de la situación más que 'llevarse bien'.

title: A feasibility and reliability pilot of a soccer-specific change-of-direction protocol incorporating ball possession, directional unpredictability, and limb dominance
abstract: Inroduction Laboratory-based change-of-direction (COD) assessments typically use predictable, ball-free tasks that inadequately reflect the perceptual and technical demands of soccer. This pilot study primarily assessed the feasibility of implementing a soccer-specific COD protocol incorporating ball possession, directional unpredictability, and limb dominance. Secondary objectives were to evaluate the intra- and inter-rater reliability of the Cutting Movement Assessment Score (CMAS) and to obtain exploratory estimates of variability in performance and biomechanical outcomes to inform the design and sample-size planning of a subsequent confirmatory trial. Methods Twenty-five trained male soccer players (Tier 2; age: 21.3 ± 1.9 years) completed eight COD conditions combining ball possession (with/without), directional predictability (predictable/unpredictable), and plant leg (dominant/non-dominant). Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, valid-trial yield, session duration, and equipment performance. Reliability of the total CMAS score was assessed using two-way random-effects, absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC₂,₁), while item-level agreement was assessed using Cohen’s κ . Preliminary outcomes included COD time, sprint-normalized COD deficit, CMAS score, peak vertical ground reaction force, peak braking force, and the horizontal-to-vertical braking force ratio. Results Recruitment efficiency was 52.1% (25 of 48 screened individuals), participant retention was 100%, and 92.7% of planned trials met the predefined validity criteria. objective: Evaluar la viabilidad de un protocolo de cambio de dirección específico de fútbol (con balón, imprevisible y por pierna dominante) y la fiabilidad de la escala CMAS.
design: Estudio piloto de viabilidad y fiabilidad, transversal, previo a un ensayo confirmatorio.
population: 25 futbolistas varones entrenados (Tier 2), 21,3 ± 1,9 años.

summary: Piloto con 25 futbolistas: un protocolo de cambio de dirección con balón e imprevisibilidad es viable y fiable de puntuar; los efectos de condición son solo exploratorios.

title: Changes in motor performance associated with a four-week rope skipping intervention in primary school children: an exploratory quasi-experimental study using the DMT 6–18
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Background Rope skipping is a scalable activity with demonstrated positive effects on children's motor coordination and physical fitness. However, little is known about its effects on overall motor performance as comprehensively assessed by the Deutscher Motorik-Test 6–18 (DMT), or which specific motor domains are most responsive to a short-term school-based rope skipping intervention. Objective This exploratory study examined changes in overall motor performance and specific motor abilities associated with a four-week Skipping Hearts rope skipping intervention in primary school children using the DMT 6–18. Methods In this quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study, 9- to 10-year-old primary school children ( n = 52; 21 intervention, 31 control) participated in either a four-week rope skipping intervention within regular physical education or continued with regular physical education (control group). Motor performance was assessed before and after the intervention using the DMT's eight standardized subtests and the DMT total score. Between-group differences in pre-post changes were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), complemented by class-level and sensitivity analyses. Reported p -values and CIs derive from individual-level analyses without adjustment for within-class dependence. Results Children in the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in overall motor performance than those in the control group [ F (1, 49) = 29.30, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.35; adjusted mean difference = 6.92 standard-score points, 95% CI (4.35, 9.50)]. Excluding jumping sideways, which differed markedly at baseline, attenuated but did not eliminate this difference [5.86 points, 95% CI (3.00, 8.72)]. title: Tactical decision-making following filanesia-based ecological dynamics in youth football through a multisite cluster-randomized trial
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: National playing philosophies can guide youth development, but whether a culturally situated framework offers lasting benefits beyond generic game-based practice remains unclear. Aims: This study compared Filanesia-based ecological dynamics (Filanesia-ED), generic ecological dynamics (Generic-ED), and conventional coaching for retained tactical decision-making, multidomain tactical adaptation, and pressure-stratified decision accuracy. Methods: A multisite three-arm cluster-randomized trial involved 144 players nested in 12 youth football teams in Lampung and North Sumatra, Indonesia. Teams completed 16 sessions over eight weeks, with assessment at pretest, posttest, and four-week retention. Analyses included longitudinal tactical outcomes, 9,806 match-decision events, 192 fidelity observations, and 1,152 small-sided-game GPS records. Player outcomes were analyzed longitudinally, and decision events were examined using generalized estimating equations. Findings were interpreted in the context of 12 randomized teams. Result: The longitudinal model showed a condition-by-time interaction, Wald χ²(4) = 363.83, p < .001. At posttest, the adjusted Filanesia-ED advantage was 12.59 points versus conventional coaching (95% CI [8.51, 16.67]) and 6.32 points versus Generic-ED (95% CI [2.25, 10.39]); corresponding retention differences were 11.33 and 6.75 points. In the event-level analysis, Filanesia-ED had higher odds of a correct decision under high opponent pressure than conventional coaching, OR = 1.74, 95% CI [1.33, 2.27], p < .001. Conclusion: Filanesia-ED was associated with higher posttest and retained tactical decision-making scores than either comparison. design: Ensayo aleatorizado por clústeres, multicéntrico, de tres brazos; 16 sesiones en 8 semanas con pretest, postest y retención a 4 semanas.

En el postest, Filanesia-ED superó al entrenamiento convencional en 12,59 puntos (IC95% 8,51–16,67) y a Generic-ED en 6,32; en retención, 11,33 y 6,75 puntos. Con alta presión rival, la probabilidad de decidir bien fue mayor que con el convencional (OR=1,74; IC95% 1,33–2,27).

title: Blocked vs. randomized practice shapes coordination across adaptation, retention, and transfer following perturbation-based balance training in young adults
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Perturbation-based balance training (PBT) improves reactive balance control, but it remains unclear whether increased practice variability, particularly the contextual interference effect (CIE), enhances retention and transfer. This study investigated whether blocked vs. randomized PBT schedules differently influence adaptation, retention, transfer, and coordination patterns. Thirty-two healthy young adults completed a single-session PBT with repeated trip perturbations under either a blocked or randomized schedule. Retention and intra-task transfer were evaluated using trained and untrained trip perturbations, and inter-task transfer was tested with a simulated forward fall. Dynamic stability performance was assessed using the margin of stability (MoS), and whole-body kinematic synergies (kSYNs) were extracted via principal component analysis to investigate coordinative changes. No significant improvements in MoS were observed during practice, and contrary to expectations derived from the CIE, randomized practice did not show superior retention, or transfer compared to blocked practice at the performance level. kSYNs revealed training-related adaptations and group differences, including changes in knee flexion contribution and stepping coordination. However, limited shared kSYNs between perturbed walking and simulated forward falls indicate strong task specificity. Together, these findings suggest that practice schedule influenced coordination patterns but did not translate into superior stability outcomes in young adults following single-session PBT.

title: "Beyond practice hours"- A systematic review of elite football development pathways.
venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
abstract: This systematic review synthesised research on the developmental activities of elite male football players and evaluated what existing evidence reveals about variation in developmental pathways across populations and contexts. Guided by the Developmental Model of Sport Participation, a framework synthesis was employed to integrate predominantly quantitative data within a qualitative, context-sensitive approach. Eighteen peer-reviewed studies were included following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, examining engagement in domain-specific activities (structured training, competition and informal play) and non-domain-specific activities (other sports). Early exposure to football was consistent across the reviewed studies, with differentiation towards elite performance emerging during adolescence through increased structured, coach-led practice. Evidence supporting early diversification was inconsistent, while engagement in informal play varied considerably across populations. Although developmental activity patterns differed between populations, the primary studies rarely measured the socio-cultural, institutional or environmental conditions potentially associated with these differences. The review extends existing knowledge by distinguishing between evidence describing what elite players did during development and evidence explaining why particular developmental pathways emerged. The findings suggest that expertise development may reflect a dynamic interaction between structured training and socio-cultural environments, supporting a context-dependent understanding of football expertise. Future research should combine developmental activity histories with direct measurements of contextual factors to better explain how different pathways to elite football emerge. PROSPERO identifier

La evidencia sobre diversificación temprana es inconsistente y el juego informal varía mucho entre poblaciones. Los estudios casi no midieron factores socioculturales.

title: Impact of Brainstorming-Driven Bounded Spaces Method on Developing Certain Creative Kinesthetic Abilities in Intermediate School Students
venue: International Journal of Experimental Sports Science Research
abstract: Backgroud: Traditional physical education instruction in soccer frequently relies on decontextualized command drills that detach motor execution from perceptual problem-solving. This study investigates the pedagogical impact of an 8-unit brainstorming-driven small-sided games curriculum (bounded spaces method) on developing fundamental soccer skills (ball control, slalom dribbling, and target shooting accuracy) and motor decision-making among male intermediate school students. Methods: A quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group pre-test/post-test design was conducted with 30 male second-intermediate students (aged 13–14 years) at Al-Haritha High School for Outstanding Students in Basra, Iraq, during the 2023–2024 academic year. Participants were assigned to an experimental group (n = 15, instructed via brainstorming-driven small-sided games across 4 weeks, 2 sessions/week, 45 min/session) or a control group (n = 15, instructed via conventional direct command drills). Skill batteries demonstrated high test-retest reliability (r = 0.86–0.89). Data were evaluated using paired and independent t-tests (df = 14 and df = 28), 95% confidence intervals, and effect size calculations (Cohen's d and Hedges' g). title: The E³P model: perception of external events and exposures in sport and exercise
venue: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
abstract: Research on perception, attention, and appraisal in sport and exercise is extensive and influential. Building on this foundation, the Integrative External Events and Exposures Perception (E³P) model is introduced as a scaffold that connects established insights and clarifies implications for research and practice. The model conceptualises perception broadly as the conversion of external events into internal information. It frames the process in three components: (a) input, encompassing sensory energies and exogenous substances that, once taken up, generate perceivable internal signals; (b) attention allocation, conceived as a depth valve that routes processing along a shallow–to–deep continuum, alongside breadth, stability, and flexibility; and (c) a four-layer sequence of meaning-making—pre-attentive perception, stimulus-driven noticing, contextual interpretation, and evaluative appraisal—that operates cumulatively and concurrently. The model outlines multiple feed-forward and feedback loops within a perception–action cycle, together with continuous interactions with proprioception, internally directed attention, and self-regulation. The model components are mapped onto five applied approaches – game-based task design, technology-mediated simulations, sensory and physiological optimisation, cognitive–attentional training, and long-term personal development – to support athlete learning and development, elite performance, and inclusive practice across diverse participants. title: “Expertise guides where attention lies”: exploring climbers’ attentional focus during route preview using eye-tracking and verbal reports
venue: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
abstract: Route preview, the visual inspection of climbing movements prior to motor execution, has attracted scientific interest over the past decades. From a sport psychology perspective, elucidating factors underlying differences in attentional focus during route preview appears promising for advancing understanding of how expertise shapes attentional processes in climbing and other relatively closed sporting contexts. This study examined attentional focus during route preview across climbers of varying skill levels by analysing gaze behaviour using portable eye-tracking. Twenty-five intermediate, advanced, and elite climbers previewed and attempted an Olympic boulder problem. Data collection included gaze behaviour during route preview alongside concurrent think-aloud and retrospective verbal reports, as well as climbing performance metrics. Besides lower climbing performance, intermediate climbers showed longer preview and total absolute fixation durations at holds than advanced and elite climbers. Despite similar overall relative fixations, the spatial distribution of these fixations differed between the groups; advanced and elite climbers displayed a more homogeneous pattern with lower variability, allocating a greater proportion of fixations to the middle and final sections of the boulder, whereas intermediate climbers focused more on the starting section. Verbal reports similarly revealed skill-level differences in attentional distribution and factors shaping attentional focus toward task-relevant holds. Findings suggest that attentional focus during route preview reflects an interplay among cognitive processing of movement demands, task difficulty relative to skill level, and perceived task-relevant priorities. title: Tactical behaviour in elite U-12 boys’ tennis: an observational mixed methods case study of the Open Super 12 Auray tournament
abstract: Evidence on tactical behaviour in elite U-12 tennis remains limited, particularly regarding how the serve interacts with rally development and point outcome. This observational mixed methods case study used a quantitatively driven qual → QUAN → qual analytical sequence to characterise the tactical profile of elite international U-12 boys competing at the 2023 Open Super 12 Auray tournament. Spontaneous match behaviours were systematically observed, transformed into coded categorical data using the OBSTENNIS-JUNIOR-S23 observational instrument, analysed quantitatively, and subsequently interpreted within their competitive and developmental context. A total of 557 points from seven matches involving eight players were analysed. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Cramér’s V, adjusted standardised residuals, and conditional winning probabilities were calculated. Point outcome was relatively balanced between server (46.7%) and receiver (53.3%). After excluding double faults, the server won 53.7% of first-serve points and 43.3% of second-serve points. Body serves predominated overall (59.4%) and were especially frequent on second serves (91.0%). Short rallies accounted for 53.1% of points, although rally length was not associated with point outcome. Unforced errors were the main route to point resolution. The integrated observational mixed methods approach enabled the construction of a contextualised tactical profile of elite U-12 boys’ tennis. These findings indicate that, in this competitive case, the serve did not provide a clear overall tactical advantage and support training approaches that combine serve-placement variability, serve–return–third-shot sequences, rally consistency, and error management.

title: Braid Complexity and Peloton Phase Dynamics
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Sport Science, Statistics, Metascience Keywords: peloton, cycling, braid complexity, phase transitions, collective behavior, Netlogo simulations A peloton is a complex, self-organizing system whose collective behavior is driven largely by energetic coupling, described by the peloton convergence ratio (PCR) and positional ordering, described here as braid complexity (C x *). We formalize peloton phase states by combining PCR with C x *, yielding a coupled energetic-positional index, C x P*. Through time-series segmentation of empirical mass-start data and NetLogo simulations, we develop a phase-space framework comprising compact, stretched, and decoupled states and associated subphases. The inclusion of directional microphases—acceleration (Da) and deceleration (Dd)—reveals a hysteresis-like asymmetry within high-PCR/low-C x * states, indicating a stretched-fatigued (Sf) state as a deceleration-driven counterpart to the standard stretched (S) phase. A multivariate approach provides a useful framework for characterizing self-organized transitions in pelotons and may help inform future study of other self-propelled biological collectives by linking individual physiological limits with group-level structural dynamics.

title: Reconfiguring coaching expertise in datafied sport: From knowledge possession to knowledge orchestration
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Although data and digital analytics are increasingly used in sport, their implications for coaching decision-making and expertise remain insufficiently understood. This study examined how data and digital analytics were incorporated into coaching judgement and decision-making and what these processes meant for the reconfiguration of coaching expertise. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with four coaches, three data and analytics specialists, and three athletes with experience in data-informed coaching in elite and professional sport. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings showed that data did not replace experiential judgement but extended what could be perceived and traced over time, while providing additional grounds on which existing assessments could be reviewed. However, greater access to information did not make coaching decisions self-evident or necessarily more objective. Participants interpreted data's meaning and limitations contextually and selectively weighted diverse forms of evidence. Interpretive work and epistemic authority were distributed among coaches, analysts, and athletes, rendering decision-making more negotiated, whereas authority and accountability for final decisions remained largely with coaches. Taken together, the findings indicated that coaching expertise was being reconfigured around the capacity to orchestrate distributed knowledge, explain, justify, and revise professional judgements, and remain accountable for decisions made under uncertainty. These findings suggest that coach education should extend beyond technical data literacy to develop capacities for contextual interpretation, knowledge orchestration, and accountable professional judgement.

title: Goalkeeper profiles in the English women's super league: Seasonal trends, team-quality contexts, and implications for coaching practice
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Goalkeeper roles in football are increasingly multidimensional, yet goalkeeper-specific evidence in elite women's football remains limited. This study examined goalkeeper match behaviours in the English Women's Super League across seven available seasons, focusing on seasonal trends and team-quality differences. Hudl StatsBomb event data covered 853 matches, 17 teams, and 71 goalkeepers. Goalkeeper actions were grouped into attacking and defensive domains, standardised using per-match and proportional metrics, and analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple factor analysis, Ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and regression models appropriate to count and cluster-membership outcomes. Attacking actions accounted for 80.92% of included goalkeeper actions. Cluster analysis identified two dominant profiles, Possession organiser and Goal defender, alongside two rare, event-defined situational subprofiles, Sweeper and Active intervener. The possession organiser profile was dominant, representing 77.7% of team-match observations, while the goal defender profile represented 15.4%. Across seasons, goalkeeper involvement showed a shift towards greater possession involvement, with increases in passing, carrying, ball receipts, and keeper-sweeper actions. Team quality was associated with differences in goalkeeper profiles: Top 4 teams showed greater possession involvement and more possession organiser profiles, whereas Low-ranking teams showed greater defensive workload and more goal defender profiles. These findings support a layered approach to goalkeeper profiling, in which broad possession- and defence-oriented involvement is interpreted alongside rare but tactically meaningful situational actions.

title: Playing up the ladder: GPS-derived match physical outputs of youth soccer players promoted to a higher age category
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: This study examined the GPS-derived match physical outputs of youth soccer players promoted to compete in a higher age category. A retrospective observational study was conducted using match data collected over three seasons (2022–23 to 2024–25) from an elite youth soccer academy (n = 221). Three questions were examined: (i) whether promoted players differed from their regular teammates when competing in their original age category; (ii) whether they differed from the regular players of the higher age category when competing alongside them; and (iii) whether the same promoted players changed their physical outputs between the two age categories. External load variables included relative total distance, high-speed running, sprint distance, high intensity accelerations and decelerations. In their original age category, promoted players did not consistently differ from their regular teammates, although promoted Under-19 midfielders covered greater high-speed running distance. In the higher age category, promoted players generally showed physical outputs similar to those of the regular players of that category, although promoted Under-19 wingers covered greater sprint distance than regular Under-23 wingers. Within-player comparisons, often based on very few players, revealed position- and category-specific changes, with significant effects for decelerations in Under-16 and Under-19 centre-backs, high-speed running and sprint distance in Under-17 full-backs and strikers, and total distance in Under-19 strikers. These findings suggest that promotion is not associated with a consistent change in match physical outputs, but rather with specific changes according to age category, playing position, and physical variable, supporting individualized approaches to player development.

title: Analysis of attacking and defensive playing styles in the Africa cup of nations under-17 and under-20 soccer tournaments
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Identifying and quantifying the different playing styles used by African youth soccer teams is important for objectively describing tactical approaches and team behaviours. This study aimed to identify and analyse team-match playing-style profiles during the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) Under-17 (U17) and Under-20 (U20) soccer tournaments. The AFCON U17 sample included 68 team-match observations from 34 matches, and the AFCON U20 sample included 60 team-match observations from 30 matches. Data were obtained from the Wyscout platform. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple factor analysis, Ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and outcome-appropriate regression models with standard errors clustered by team and match. The pooled analysis identified four team-match profiles: (1) limited progression, (2) controlled possession and progression, (3) balanced counterattacking, and (4) direct high-transition duel. Pooled Clusters 2 and 3 had higher estimated goal rates than Clusters 1 and 4 after adjustment for multiple comparisons, and U20 teams had a lower estimated goal rate than U17 teams. No pairwise differences in winning odds between clusters remained significant after adjustment, and no robust association was identified between cluster membership and goals conceded. The findings, therefore, provide stronger evidence for an association with goals scored than with match outcome.

title: Talent or timing? Skeletal maturity, biological maturation, and the relative age effect in youth athletes: a cross-sectional study from a high-performance sporting environment
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Aim We characterised the skeletal maturity profile, relative age distribution, and sport-type differences in biological maturation within a cohort of selected youth athletes from a high-performance sport environment. Methods Thirty-seven youth athletes (20 male, 17 female; mean chronological age: 14.92 ± 1.81 years) from 21 clubs across 15 sports in Split, Croatia, were assessed during the 2024–2025 competitive season. Skeletal age (SA) was estimated using the validated BAUSport™ SonicBone ultrasound system and compared with chronological age (CA). Athletes were classified as early (SA-CA ≥ + 1.0 year), on-time, or late maturers. Sports were assigned a priori to physical/power-dominant or skill/technical-aesthetic categories. The Relative Age Effect (RAE) was examined via chi-square goodness-of-fit and pairwise odds ratios; the primary sport-type contrast used the Mann–Whitney U test with rank-biserial r as the effect size index. Results Mean SA exceeded CA by 0.77 ± 0.89 years across the cohort, with 29.7% classified as early maturers and only 2.7% as late maturers. title: Auditory deprivation impairs badminton players’ stroke and anticipatory performance: a field experimental study
abstract: Background Accurate anticipation and precise motor execution are critical to success in badminton, yet most previous research has focused on visual information, with limited evidence regarding the role of auditory information. The present study used a two-part field design to investigate the effects of auditory information on stroke performance and anticipatory performance in badminton. Methods Thirty skilled badminton players completed both parts of the study in a fixed sequence. Part A employed a within-subjects design to examine the effects of modality type (audiovisual condition vs. visual-only condition) on reaction time and hitting accuracy in a smash-return task under the predictable-shot context (shot depth and direction known in advance). Part B employed the same participants and experimental design, with the addition of eye-tracking technology, to examine the effects of modality type on reaction time, mean fixation duration, and saccade frequency under an anticipatory condition (shot depth and direction unknown). Results In Part A, auditory deprivation significantly reduced stroke scores ( p < 0.001) and increased failure rates ( p < 0.001), but did not affect reaction time ( p = 0.376). Conclusion Auditory deprivation led to declines in both stroke accuracy and anticipatory efficiency in badminton players, indicating that auditory information may play a significant role in athletes’ motor control and perceptual processing.
